15"""Ascend (910B) backend for torch.linalg.matrix_rank. 

16 

17The upstream GPU implementation (src/flag_gems/ops/linalg_matrix_rank.py) is a 

18pure-Triton SVD: one-sided Jacobi for small/medium matrices, Householder 

19tridiagonalization / bidiagonalization + Sturm bisection for large ones. It is 

20deeply CUDA-specific (``_sm_count`` queries ``torch.cuda`` streaming 

21multiprocessors; the blocked paths synchronize with atomic-based software grid 

22barriers that have no equivalent on triton-ascend). 

23 

24This file ports that algorithm to triton-ascend in stages. Small matrices 

25use closed-form rank1/rank2 kernels; fp32 matrices with k <= 32 use a 

26single fused Golub-Kahan bidiagonalization + register Sturm kernel; 

27hermitian fp32 matrices with 32 < k <= 64 use a padded one-sided 

28tridiagonalization + Sturm count; other fp32 matrices with k <= 64 use a 

29single-program Golub-Kahan bidiagonalization (m, n <= 64) or, for long 

30dimensions, a Householder QR compression to the k x k R factor (backward 

31stable in the linear sigma domain) followed by the same bidiagonalization 

32-- both ending in the shared Sturm tail whose decisive count runs in 

33double-single (df64) arithmetic from the raw bidiagonal d/e; fp32 matrices 

34with 64 < k <= 255 use the same exact paths BY DEFAULT (the 

35tridiagonalization / bidiagonalization below). For non-hermitian inputs whose 

36long dimension exceeds 256, FLAGGEMS_MR_FAST_PATH=1 opts into a pure-Triton 

37blocked Householder QR (unpivoted) whose |R_ii| diagonal is counted against 

38the tolerance: 

39rank = #{ |R_ii| > max(atol, rtol * sigma_max) }, with sigma_max 

40bracketed by |R_00| and ||A||_F and refined by power iteration only when 

41the two bounds disagree; and fp32 matrices with k > 255 ALWAYS use an 

42unblocked Golub-Kahan bidiagonalization (non-hermitian) or a one-sided 

43Householder tridiagonalization (hermitian -- half the reflectors of 

44Golub-Kahan), plus a Sturm count whose decisive pass runs in 

45double-single (df64) arithmetic (SVD-accurate); hermitian ranks are 

46counted in the eigenvalue domain by a +/-tol double-chain Sturm bracket. 

47The exact paths are the DEFAULT; FLAGGEMS_MR_FAST_PATH=1 opts back into 

48the fast approximations (Gram sigma^2-domain count for long-dimension 

49k <= 64, unpivoted-QR |R_ii| count for non-hermitian 64 < k <= 255 with 

50rows > 256), which are faster but less accurate on adversarial spectra. 

51fp64 is rejected with NotImplementedError (this toolchain cannot compile 

52fp64 Triton kernels); there is no aclnn/native decomposition fallback 

53anywhere -- every rank is computed by the Triton kernels in this file (the 

54hermitian 32 < k <= 64 path only uses host-side aten ops -- zeros / where / 

55arange -- for padding and lower-triangle symmetrization, never for the 

56decomposition itself). Empty inputs still validate tolerance 

57dtype/device/broadcast before returning (native torch validates before 

58its empty-input return too). Every non-empty call is scale-normalized at 

59the entry: each batch matrix is divided by its lower-triangle 

60(hermitian) / full-matrix max-abs and atol by the same factor, so fp32 

61sum-of-squares neither overflow (|x| ~ 1e20) nor underflow (|x| ~ 1e-30); 

62rank semantics are invariant under the scaling (rtol is relative). 

63 

64Implementation note: the RRQR kernels below are extremely sensitive to this 

65toolchain's codegen instabilities; the inline comments document every 

66workaround (they are load-bearing -- do not "clean them up"). 

67"""

90def _sm_count(device): 

91 """Number of vector cores available on the Ascend device. 

92 

93 Replaces the GPU ``_sm_count`` (which queried CUDA streaming multiprocessor 

94 count). triton-ascend exposes the AI-core / vector-core topology through 

95 ``triton.runtime.driver``; 910B4 has 20 AI cores x 2 vector sub-cores = 40. 

96 """ 

97 index = device.index 

98 if index is None: 

99 index = torch.npu.current_device() 

100 count = _VEC_CORE_CACHE.get(index) 

101 if count is None: 

102 try: 

103 from triton.runtime import driver 

104 

105 props = driver.active.utils.get_device_properties(index) 

106 count = props.get("num_vectorcore", 40) if isinstance(props, dict) else 40 

107 except Exception: 

108 count = 40 

109 _VEC_CORE_CACHE[index] = count 

110 return count

114# Dispatch thresholds (ported from the shared GPU op) 

115# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

116# Fused single-program Jacobi covers small/medium matrices; everything larger 

117# falls through to the placeholder (and, in later stages, the blocked paths). 

118_FUSED_JACOBI_MAX_K = 64 

119_FUSED_JACOBI_MAX_K_FP64 = 32 

120_FUSED_JACOBI_MAX_ROWS = 256 

121_FUSED_JACOBI_WIDE_MAX_ROWS = 128 

122 

123# Small/medium path (fp32, k <= 64, any row count): fused kernel for 

124# m,n <= 32, bidiag64 for the non-hermitian 33..64 band, padded 

125# tridiagonalization for hermitian 33..64, QR-compression to the k x k R 

126# factor + bidiag64 for long dimensions. 

127_TRIDIAG_MAX_K = 64 

128_RRQR_MAX_K = 255 

129# CANN 9.1.1 cannot compile the register-panel specializations needed by 

130# compact 65..255 QR. The GM-panel QR remains useful only for non-hermitian 

131# long-row inputs; compact inputs and every hermitian input stay on the exact 

132# bidiagonalization/tridiagonalization paths even when FAST_PATH=1. 

133_RRQR_FAST_MIN_ROWS = 257 

134 

135# CANN 9.1.1/BiShengIR UB-overflows both the NB=2 and NB=4 specializations of 

136# the register-resident QR panel. The active QR launch domains all have more 

137# than 64 rows, so they use the GM-tile panel; keep NB=1 available for future 

138# callers/toolchains without exposing a known-uncompilable path. 

139_RRQR_REG_PANEL_MAX_ROWS = 64

142def _jacobi_sweeps(k, is_fp64): 

143 """Worst-case sweep cap; kernels exit early once the Weyl bound holds.""" 

144 if is_fp64: 

145 if k <= 16: 

146 return 12 

147 if k <= 32: 

148 return 16 

149 if k <= 256: 

150 return 18 

151 return 24 

152 if k <= 16: 

153 return 8 

154 if k <= 32: 

155 return 12 

156 if k <= 256: 

157 return 14 

158 return 18

161# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

162# Tolerance / validation helpers (ported verbatim from the shared op) 

163# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

164def _expand_tolerance(value, batch_count, batch_shape, input, name): 

165 """Return a flat (batch_count,) tolerance tensor. 

166 

167 Kept flat (always >= 1-D) on purpose: under ``use_gems()`` every factory 

168 op is patched to the Ascend backend, and the Ascend ``full_like`` kernel 

169 rejects 0-D (scalar) tensors (it requires a SUBBLOCK_SIZE it cannot derive 

170 for an empty grid). A non-batched input has ``batch_shape == ()``; working 

171 in the flattened (batch_count,) space avoids that 0-D recursion entirely. 

172 """ 

173 if isinstance(value, torch.Tensor): 

174 if value.is_complex(): 

175 raise RuntimeError( 

176 f"torch.linalg.matrix_rank: {name} tensor of complex type is not " 

177 f"supported. Got {value.dtype}" 

178 ) 

179 if value.device != input.device: 

180 raise RuntimeError( 

181 f"torch.linalg.matrix_rank: Expected {name} and input tensors to " 

182 f"be on the same device, but got {name} on {value.device} and " 

183 f"input on {input.device}" 

184 ) 

185 try: 

186 value = value.expand(batch_shape) 

187 except RuntimeError as error: 

188 raise RuntimeError( 

189 f"torch.linalg.matrix_rank: {name} with shape {tuple(value.shape)} " 

190 f"is not broadcastable to batch shape {tuple(batch_shape)}" 

191 ) from error 

192 return value.to(dtype=input.dtype).contiguous().reshape(batch_count) 

193 

194 try: 

195 scalar = float(value) 

196 except (TypeError, ValueError) as error: 

197 raise TypeError( 

198 f"torch.linalg.matrix_rank: {name} must be a float or Tensor" 

199 ) from error 

200 return torch.full((batch_count,), scalar, dtype=input.dtype, device=input.device) 

201 

202 

203def _prepare_tolerances(input, atol, rtol): 

204 m, n = input.shape[-2], input.shape[-1] 

205 batch_shape = input.shape[:-2] 

206 batch_count = input.numel() // (m * n) 

207 atol_is_set = atol is not None 

208 atol_tensor = _expand_tolerance( 

209 0.0 if atol is None else atol, batch_count, batch_shape, input, "atol" 

210 ) 

211 

212 if rtol is not None: 

213 rtol_tensor = _expand_tolerance(rtol, batch_count, batch_shape, input, "rtol") 

214 else: 

215 default_rtol = max(m, n) * torch.finfo(input.dtype).eps 

216 if atol_is_set: 

217 rtol_tensor = torch.where( 

218 atol_tensor > 0, 

219 torch.zeros((batch_count,), dtype=input.dtype, device=input.device), 

220 torch.full( 

221 (batch_count,), 

222 default_rtol, 

223 dtype=input.dtype, 

224 device=input.device, 

225 ), 

226 ) 

227 else: 

228 rtol_tensor = torch.full( 

229 (batch_count,), 

230 default_rtol, 

231 dtype=input.dtype, 

232 device=input.device, 

233 ) 

234 

235 return atol_tensor, rtol_tensor.contiguous() 

236 

237 

238def _tolerance_scalars(input, atol, rtol): 

239 """Scalar fast path mirroring _prepare_tolerances for non-tensor 

240 atol/rtol: returns plain floats so the kernels can receive the 

241 tolerances as scalar arguments instead of materialized (batch,) 

242 tensors (saves two fill-kernel launches per call).""" 

243 m, n = input.shape[-2], input.shape[-1] 

244 try: 

245 atol_val = 0.0 if atol is None else float(atol) 

246 except (TypeError, ValueError) as error: 

247 raise TypeError( 

248 "torch.linalg.matrix_rank: atol must be a float or Tensor" 

249 ) from error 

250 if rtol is not None: 

251 try: 

252 rtol_val = float(rtol) 

253 except (TypeError, ValueError) as error: 

254 raise TypeError( 

255 "torch.linalg.matrix_rank: rtol must be a float or Tensor" 

256 ) from error 

257 else: 

258 default_rtol = max(m, n) * torch.finfo(input.dtype).eps 

259 # torch semantics: an explicitly set positive atol suppresses the 

260 # default rtol (mirrors the torch.where branch in 

261 # _prepare_tolerances). 

262 rtol_val = 0.0 if (atol is not None and atol_val > 0) else default_rtol 

263 return atol_val, rtol_val 

264 

265 

266def _validate_tolerance_metadata(input, atol, rtol): 

267 """Host-side-only tolerance validation for the empty-input early return 

268 (which never calls _prepare_tolerances -- that would divide by 

269 m*n == 0). Mirrors _expand_tolerance's checks so empty inputs reject 

270 invalid tolerances exactly like non-empty ones (native torch validates 

271 tolerances before its empty-input return as well).""" 

272 batch_shape = input.shape[:-2] 

273 for name, value in (("atol", atol), ("rtol", rtol)): 

274 if value is None: 

275 continue 

276 if not isinstance(value, torch.Tensor): 

277 try: 

278 float(value) 

279 except (TypeError, ValueError) as error: 

280 raise TypeError( 

281 f"torch.linalg.matrix_rank: {name} must be a float or Tensor" 

282 ) from error 

283 continue 

284 if value.is_complex(): 

285 raise RuntimeError( 

286 f"torch.linalg.matrix_rank: {name} tensor of complex type is " 

287 f"not supported. Got {value.dtype}" 

288 ) 

289 if value.device != input.device: 

290 raise RuntimeError( 

291 f"torch.linalg.matrix_rank: Expected {name} and input tensors " 

292 f"to be on the same device, but got {name} on {value.device} " 

293 f"and input on {input.device}" 

294 ) 

295 try: 

296 value.expand(batch_shape) 

297 except RuntimeError as error: 

298 raise RuntimeError( 

299 f"torch.linalg.matrix_rank: {name} with shape " 

300 f"{tuple(value.shape)} is not broadcastable to batch shape " 

301 f"{tuple(batch_shape)}" 

302 ) from error 

303 

304 

305def _check_input(input, hermitian): 

306 if input.ndim < 2: 

307 raise RuntimeError( 

308 "torch.linalg.matrix_rank: input must have at least 2 dimensions" 

309 ) 

310 if input.dtype not in (torch.float32, torch.float64): 

311 raise NotImplementedError( 

312 "FlagGems linalg_matrix_rank currently supports float32 and float64 " 

313 f"real inputs only; got {input.dtype}" 

314 ) 

315 if hermitian and input.shape[-2] != input.shape[-1]: 

316 raise RuntimeError( 

317 "torch.linalg.matrix_rank: A must be batches of square matrices when " 

318 "hermitian=True" 

319 ) 

320 

321 

322def _empty_matrix_rank(input, output_shape): 

323 out = torch.empty(output_shape, dtype=torch.int64, device=input.device) 

324 output_size = out.numel() 

325 if output_size: 

326 block_size = min(256, triton.next_power_of_2(output_size)) 

327 with torch_device_fn.device(input.device): 

328 _matrix_rank_zero_kernel[(triton.cdiv(output_size, block_size),)]( 

329 out, 

330 N=output_size, 

331 BLOCK_SIZE=block_size, 

332 ) 

333 return out 

334 

335 

336def _copy_rank_to_out(input, result, out): 

337 if out is None: 

338 raise TypeError("torch.linalg.matrix_rank: out must be a Tensor") 

339 if out.device != input.device: 

340 raise RuntimeError( 

341 "torch.linalg.matrix_rank: Expected result and input tensors to be on " 

342 f"the same device, but got result on {out.device} and input on " 

343 f"{input.device}" 

344 ) 

345 if not torch.can_cast(result.dtype, out.dtype): 

346 raise RuntimeError( 

347 "torch.linalg.matrix_rank: Expected result to be safely castable from " 

348 f"Long dtype, but got result with dtype {result.dtype}" 

349 ) 

350 

351 if out.numel() != 0 and out.shape != result.shape: 

352 warnings.warn( 

353 "An output with one or more elements was resized because it had shape " 

354 f"{tuple(out.shape)}, which does not match the required output shape " 

355 f"{tuple(result.shape)}.", 

356 UserWarning, 

357 stacklevel=3, 

358 ) 

359 out.resize_(result.shape) 

360 out.copy_(result) 

361 return out

364# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

365# Kernels 

366# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

367@libentry() 

368@triton.jit 

369def _matrix_rank_zero_kernel(out, N: tl.constexpr, BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr): 

370 offsets = tl.program_id(0) * BLOCK_SIZE + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE) 

371 tl.store(out + offsets, 0, mask=offsets < N) 

372 

373 

374@triton.jit 

375def _mr_normalize_small_kernel( 

376 A, 

377 OUT, 

378 SCALE, 

379 FLAG, 

380 M: tl.constexpr, 

381 N: tl.constexpr, 

382 HERMITIAN: tl.constexpr, 

383 NEED_FLAG: tl.constexpr, 

384 BLOCK_R: tl.constexpr, 

385 BLOCK_C: tl.constexpr, 

386): 

387 # Single-launch scale normalization for small matrices (m, n <= 64): 

388 # per-batch power-of-two max-abs scale + in-kernel divide. The aten 

389 # equivalent (abs -> amax -> mantissa mask -> where -> div, plus tril 

390 # for hermitian) costs 5-6 launches, which dominates sub-millisecond 

391 # ops. HERMITIAN takes the scale from the LOWER triangle only (torch 

392 # reads just the lower triangle; garbage above the diagonal must not 

393 # inflate the scale) while still writing out the FULL scaled matrix. 

394 # The bit trick zeroes the fp32 mantissa -> the divisor is 2^e and the 

395 # division is exact; a masked-to-zero scale (all-zero or subnormal-max 

396 # matrix) maps to 1, i.e. "no scaling", matching native torch. FLAG 

397 # (written only under NEED_FLAG, for the tensor-tolerance negative-tol 

398 # fixup) records "the (lower-triangle) max-abs is nonzero", sparing the 

399 # fixup its own full-matrix amax/amin/tril scan. 

400 batch = tl.program_id(0) 

401 rr = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_R)[:, None] 

402 cc = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_C)[None, :] 

403 lmask = (rr < M) & (cc < N) 

404 a = tl.load(A + batch * M * N + rr * N + cc, mask=lmask, other=0.0) 

405 aa = tl.abs(a) 

406 if HERMITIAN: 

407 aa = tl.where(rr >= cc, aa, 0.0) 

408 row_max = tl.max(aa, axis=1) # (BLOCK_R,), >= 0 

409 if NEED_FLAG: 

410 nz = tl.max(row_max, axis=0) > 0.0 

411 tl.store(FLAG + batch, nz.to(tl.int8)) 

412 # pow2-floor per row, then the batch max: pow2_floor is monotonic on 

413 # nonneg floats, so pow2_floor(max) == max(pow2_floor(row_maxes)) -- 

414 # this keeps the bitcast on a VECTOR (a scalar bitcast miscompiles on 

415 # this backend). 

416 pw = (row_max.to(tl.int32, bitcast=True) & -8388608).to(tl.float32, bitcast=True) 

417 scale = tl.max(pw, axis=0) 

418 scale = tl.where(scale > 0, scale, 1.0) 

419 tl.store(SCALE + batch, scale) 

420 tl.store(OUT + batch * M * N + rr * N + cc, a / scale, mask=lmask) 

421 

422 

423# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

424# rank-1 / rank-2 special cases (single program per matrix, no barrier) 

425# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

426@libentry() 

427@triton.jit 

428def _matrix_rank_rank1_kernel( 

429 A, 

430 ATOL, 

431 RTOL, 

432 OUT, 

433 ATOL_VAL, 

434 RTOL_VAL, 

435 M: tl.constexpr, 

436 N: tl.constexpr, 

437 ROWS: tl.constexpr, 

438 TALL: tl.constexpr, 

439 HERMITIAN: tl.constexpr, 

440 BLOCK_R: tl.constexpr, 

441 TOL_TENSOR: tl.constexpr, 

442): 

443 batch = tl.program_id(0) 

444 rows = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_R) 

445 row_mask = rows < ROWS 

446 a_base = A + batch * M * N 

447 

448 if HERMITIAN: 

449 values = tl.load(a_base + rows * N, mask=row_mask, other=0.0) 

450 elif TALL: 

451 values = tl.load(a_base + rows * N, mask=row_mask, other=0.0) 

452 else: 

453 values = tl.load(a_base + rows, mask=row_mask, other=0.0) 

454 

455 singular_value = tl.sqrt(tl.sum(values * values, axis=0)) 

456 if TOL_TENSOR: 

457 atol = tl.load(ATOL + batch) 

458 rtol = tl.load(RTOL + batch) 

459 else: 

460 atol = ATOL_VAL 

461 rtol = RTOL_VAL 

462 threshold = tl.maximum(atol, rtol * singular_value) 

463 rank = (singular_value > threshold).to(tl.int64) 

464 tl.store(OUT + batch, rank) 

465 

466 

467@libentry() 

468@triton.jit 

469def _matrix_rank_rank2_kernel( 

470 A, 

471 ATOL, 

472 RTOL, 

473 OUT, 

474 ATOL_VAL, 

475 RTOL_VAL, 

476 M: tl.constexpr, 

477 N: tl.constexpr, 

478 ROWS: tl.constexpr, 

479 TALL: tl.constexpr, 

480 HERMITIAN: tl.constexpr, 

481 BLOCK_R: tl.constexpr, 

482 REL_EPS: tl.constexpr, 

483 ABS_EPS: tl.constexpr, 

484 TOL_TENSOR: tl.constexpr, 

485): 

486 batch = tl.program_id(0) 

487 rows = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_R) 

488 row_mask = rows < ROWS 

489 a_base = A + batch * M * N 

490 

491 if HERMITIAN: 

492 x = tl.load(a_base + rows * N, mask=row_mask, other=0.0) 

493 lower_rows = tl.maximum(rows, 1) 

494 lower_columns = tl.minimum(rows, 1) 

495 y = tl.load(a_base + lower_rows * N + lower_columns, mask=row_mask, other=0.0) 

496 elif TALL: 

497 x = tl.load(a_base + rows * N, mask=row_mask, other=0.0) 

498 y = tl.load(a_base + rows * N + 1, mask=row_mask, other=0.0) 

499 else: 

500 x = tl.load(a_base + rows, mask=row_mask, other=0.0) 

501 y = tl.load(a_base + N + rows, mask=row_mask, other=0.0) 

502 

503 alpha = tl.sum(x * x, axis=0) 

504 beta = tl.sum(y * y, axis=0) 

505 gamma = tl.sum(x * y, axis=0) 

506 active = tl.abs(gamma) > REL_EPS * tl.sqrt(alpha * beta + ABS_EPS) 

507 safe_gamma = tl.where(active, gamma, 1.0) 

508 tau = (beta - alpha) / (2.0 * safe_gamma) 

509 sign_tau = tl.where(tau >= 0.0, 1.0, -1.0) 

510 t = sign_tau / (tl.abs(tau) + tl.sqrt(1.0 + tau * tau)) 

511 c = 1.0 / tl.sqrt(1.0 + t * t) 

512 s = t * c 

513 c = tl.where(active, c, 1.0) 

514 s = tl.where(active, s, 0.0) 

515 

516 rotated_x = c * x - s * y 

517 rotated_y = s * x + c * y 

518 singular_x = tl.sqrt(tl.sum(rotated_x * rotated_x, axis=0)) 

519 singular_y = tl.sqrt(tl.sum(rotated_y * rotated_y, axis=0)) 

520 max_value = tl.maximum(singular_x, singular_y) 

521 

522 if TOL_TENSOR: 

523 atol = tl.load(ATOL + batch) 

524 rtol = tl.load(RTOL + batch) 

525 else: 

526 atol = ATOL_VAL 

527 rtol = RTOL_VAL 

528 threshold = tl.maximum(atol, rtol * max_value) 

529 rank = (singular_x > threshold).to(tl.int32) 

530 rank += (singular_y > threshold).to(tl.int32) 

531 tl.store(OUT + batch, rank.to(tl.int64)) 

532 

533 

534# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

535# Fused one-sided cyclic Jacobi (single program per matrix, no grid barrier). 

536# Computes singular values entirely in Triton (no aclnn SVD), so it works for 

537# both fp32 and fp64. Native rotation math is used for both dtypes (the GPU 

538# df32/df64 refinement is a speed optimization for weak-FP64 GPUs and is not 

539# needed for Ascend correctness). 

540# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

541@libentry() 

542@triton.jit 

543def _matrix_rank_fused_jacobi_kernel( 

544 A, 

545 A_WORK, 

546 ATOL, 

547 RTOL, 

548 OUT, 

549 BATCH_COUNT: tl.constexpr, 

550 M: tl.constexpr, 

551 N: tl.constexpr, 

552 K: tl.constexpr, 

553 ROWS: tl.constexpr, 

554 TALL: tl.constexpr, 

555 HERMITIAN: tl.constexpr, 

556 IS_FP64: tl.constexpr, 

557 ROUND: tl.constexpr, 

558 PAIRS: tl.constexpr, 

559 BLOCK_R: tl.constexpr, 

560 BLOCK_P: tl.constexpr, 

561 BLOCK_K: tl.constexpr, 

562 BLOCK_C: tl.constexpr, 

563 SWEEPS, 

564 REL_EPS: tl.constexpr, 

565 ABS_EPS: tl.constexpr, 

566): 

567 # The work matrix round-trips through global memory each Jacobi step. On 

568 # Ascend a program's MTE3 stores and MTE2 loads are unordered, and under 

569 # cross-program congestion the store->load races (flaky wrong ranks). A 

570 # single resident program is fine -- the inner ``tl.debug_barrier`` restores 

571 # ordering -- so the whole batch is processed serially by one program 

572 # (grid=(1,)). This trades batch throughput for determinism. 

573 rows = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_R) 

574 row_mask = rows < ROWS 

575 for batch in range(BATCH_COUNT): 

576 a_base = A + batch * M * N 

577 work_base = A_WORK + batch * K * ROWS 

578 

579 # Load the working matrix: column j of W is column/row j of A. 

580 column = 0 

581 while column < K: 

582 if HERMITIAN: 

583 source_rows = tl.maximum(rows, column) 

584 source_columns = tl.minimum(rows, column) 

585 values = tl.load( 

586 a_base + source_rows * N + source_columns, 

587 mask=row_mask, 

588 other=0.0, 

589 ) 

590 elif TALL: 

591 values = tl.load(a_base + rows * N + column, mask=row_mask, other=0.0) 

592 else: 

593 values = tl.load(a_base + column * N + rows, mask=row_mask, other=0.0) 

594 tl.store(work_base + column * ROWS + rows, values, mask=row_mask) 

595 column += 1 

596 

597 pair = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_P) 

598 ring: tl.constexpr = ROUND - 1 

599 accumulator_dtype = tl.float64 if IS_FP64 else tl.float32 

600 singular_indices = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_K) 

601 atol = tl.load(ATOL + batch) 

602 rtol = tl.load(RTOL + batch) 

603 sweep = 0 

604 e2_prev = tl.zeros((), dtype=accumulator_dtype) 

605 alphas = tl.zeros((BLOCK_K,), dtype=accumulator_dtype) 

606 keep_sweeping = 1 

607 while (sweep < SWEEPS) & (keep_sweeping != 0): 

608 rotations = 0 

609 e2_local = tl.zeros((), dtype=accumulator_dtype) 

610 step = 0 

611 while step < ROUND - 1: 

612 position_q = ROUND - 1 - pair 

613 p = tl.where(pair == 0, 0, ((pair + ring - step - 1) % ring) + 1) 

614 q = tl.where( 

615 position_q == 0, 0, ((position_q + ring - step - 1) % ring) + 1 

616 ) 

617 valid_pair = (pair < PAIRS) & (p < K) & (q < K) 

618 swap = p > q 

619 ordered_p = tl.where(swap, q, p) 

620 ordered_q = tl.where(swap, p, q) 

621 pair_mask = valid_pair[:, None] & row_mask[None, :] 

622 

623 ap = tl.load( 

624 work_base + ordered_p[:, None] * ROWS + rows[None, :], 

625 mask=pair_mask, 

626 other=0.0, 

627 ) 

628 aq = tl.load( 

629 work_base + ordered_q[:, None] * ROWS + rows[None, :], 

630 mask=pair_mask, 

631 other=0.0, 

632 ) 

633 alpha = tl.sum(ap * ap, axis=1) 

634 beta = tl.sum(aq * aq, axis=1) 

635 gamma = tl.sum(ap * aq, axis=1) 

636 e2_local += tl.sum(gamma * gamma, axis=0).to(accumulator_dtype) 

637 

638 active = valid_pair & ( 

639 tl.abs(gamma) > REL_EPS * tl.sqrt(alpha * beta + ABS_EPS) 

640 ) 

641 safe_gamma = tl.where(active, gamma, 1.0) 

642 tau = (beta - alpha) / (2.0 * safe_gamma) 

643 sign_tau = tl.where(tau >= 0.0, 1.0, -1.0) 

644 t = sign_tau / (tl.abs(tau) + tl.sqrt(1.0 + tau * tau)) 

645 c = 1.0 / tl.sqrt(1.0 + t * t) 

646 s = t * c 

647 

648 rotations += tl.sum(active.to(tl.int32), axis=0) 

649 c = tl.where(active, c, 1.0) 

650 s = tl.where(active, s, 0.0) 

651 # Gate the write on ``active``: inactive pairs would only 

652 # rewrite identical values, so skipping the store avoids a 

653 # needless store->load round-trip. 

654 write_mask = pair_mask & active[:, None] 

655 tl.store( 

656 work_base + ordered_p[:, None] * ROWS + rows[None, :], 

657 c[:, None] * ap - s[:, None] * aq, 

658 mask=write_mask, 

659 ) 

660 tl.store( 

661 work_base + ordered_q[:, None] * ROWS + rows[None, :], 

662 s[:, None] * ap + c[:, None] * aq, 

663 mask=write_mask, 

664 ) 

665 tl.debug_barrier() 

666 step += 1 

667 

668 # Rank-stability check (Weyl bound): once the residual off-diagonal 

669 # energy cannot move a singular value across tol, stop early. 

670 check_tile = tl.load( 

671 work_base + singular_indices[:, None] * ROWS + rows[None, :], 

672 mask=(singular_indices < K)[:, None] & row_mask[None, :], 

673 other=0.0, 

674 ) 

675 alphas = tl.sum(check_tile * check_tile, axis=1).to(accumulator_dtype) 

676 maxa = tl.max(alphas, axis=0) 

677 tol = tl.maximum(atol, rtol * tl.sqrt(maxa)) 

678 tol2 = tol * tol 

679 margin = tl.min( 

680 tl.where( 

681 singular_indices < K, 

682 tl.abs(alphas - tol2), 

683 tl.full((BLOCK_K,), float("inf"), dtype=accumulator_dtype), 

684 ), 

685 axis=0, 

686 ) 

687 stall_floor = 64.0 * REL_EPS * maxa 

688 stable = (e2_local <= 0.25 * margin * margin) | ( 

689 (sweep > 0) 

690 & (e2_local >= 0.8 * e2_prev) 

691 & (e2_local <= stall_floor * stall_floor) 

692 ) 

693 e2_prev = e2_local 

694 keep_sweeping = ((rotations != 0) & (stable == 0)).to(tl.int32) 

695 sweep += 1 

696 

697 singular_values = tl.sqrt(alphas) 

698 max_value = tl.max(singular_values, axis=0) 

699 threshold = tl.maximum(atol, rtol * max_value) 

700 rank = tl.sum( 

701 ((singular_values > threshold) & (singular_indices < K)).to(tl.int32), 

702 axis=0, 

703 ) 

704 tl.store(OUT + batch, rank.to(tl.int64)) 

705 

706 

707# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

708# Medium matrices (k <= 64): Gram via Cube + Householder tridiagonalization + 

709# Sturm-sequence eigenvalue counting (non-iterative, one program per batch 

710# element). The trailing matrix stays register/UB-resident for the whole 

711# reduction -- there is no global-memory store->load round trip inside it, so 

712# the Ascend MTE3(store)/MTE2(load) reordering hazard that made the 

713# GM-resident Jacobi sweep flaky under batch concurrency cannot occur, and 

714# the batch is fully parallel (grid = batch_count). 

715# 

716# Toolchain notes (all verified on this machine): 

717# * tl.dot only accepts operands that are direct loads (or dot chains), so 

718# the Gram matrix is built in a separate kernel and reloaded below. 

719# * DSA extract_slice/insert_slice and axis-0 register-tile reductions both 

720# crash or hang the Ascend backend here; everything below is expressed as 

721# full-tile elementwise ops plus axis-1 reductions. 

722# * `tl.arange(...) == const` masks miscompile (device exception); masks are 

723# written as strict-inequality intervals: (x == c) -> (x > c-1) & (x < c+1). 

724# * By symmetry g[j, j+1:] == g[j+1:, j], so the Householder vector is taken 

725# from the COLUMN below the diagonal, which an axis-1 reduction can 

726# extract from a full tile without any gather. 

727# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

728 

729 

730@triton.jit 

731def _sturm_count_less(D, E, base, K: tl.constexpr, x): 

732 """Number of eigenvalues of the symmetric tridiagonal T = diag(d) + 

733 diag(e, +/-1) that are <= x, via the qd recurrence (LAPACK DLANEG 

734 convention: a zero pivot is replaced by a tiny negative value so the 

735 count stays consistent for clustered spectra). Runs in fp32: the qd 

736 quotients stay on the scale of (d - x), so no overflow for the matrix 

737 magnitudes this path handles.""" 

738 q = tl.load(D + base) - x 

739 q = tl.where(q == 0.0, -1.1754944e-38, q) 

740 neg = (q < 0.0).to(tl.int32) 

741 i = 1 

742 while i < K: 

743 di = tl.load(D + base + i) 

744 ei = tl.load(E + base + i - 1) 

745 q = (di - x) - ei * ei / q 

746 q = tl.where(q == 0.0, -1.1754944e-38, q) 

747 neg += (q < 0.0).to(tl.int32) 

748 i += 1 

749 return neg 

750 

751 

752@triton.jit 

753def _sturm_count_less2(D, E, base, K: tl.constexpr, x1, x2): 

754 """Lockstep pair of _sturm_count_less: two thresholds in ONE pass of the 

755 qd recurrence. The sequential K-step chain dominates the Sturm kernel's 

756 latency and the bracketing needs two (hermitian: four) counts, so pairing 

757 halves the serial work. Identical fp32 semantics to two separate 

758 calls.""" 

759 d0 = tl.load(D + base) 

760 q1 = d0 - x1 

761 q2 = d0 - x2 

762 q1 = tl.where(q1 == 0.0, -1.1754944e-38, q1) 

763 q2 = tl.where(q2 == 0.0, -1.1754944e-38, q2) 

764 neg1 = (q1 < 0.0).to(tl.int32) 

765 neg2 = (q2 < 0.0).to(tl.int32) 

766 i = 1 

767 while i < K: 

768 di = tl.load(D + base + i) 

769 ei = tl.load(E + base + i - 1) 

770 e2 = ei * ei 

771 q1 = (di - x1) - e2 / q1 

772 q2 = (di - x2) - e2 / q2 

773 q1 = tl.where(q1 == 0.0, -1.1754944e-38, q1) 

774 q2 = tl.where(q2 == 0.0, -1.1754944e-38, q2) 

775 neg1 += (q1 < 0.0).to(tl.int32) 

776 neg2 += (q2 < 0.0).to(tl.int32) 

777 i += 1 

778 return neg1, neg2 

779 

780 

781@triton.jit 

782def _sturm_count_strict(D, E, base, K: tl.constexpr, x): 

783 """STRICT variant of _sturm_count_less: counts #{lambda < x}. Same qd 

784 recurrence, but the zero-pivot guard replaces a zero pivot with a tiny 

785 POSITIVE value -- the mirrored DLANEG tie convention -- so an eigenvalue 

786 exactly equal to x is NOT counted. Used for the hermitian negative side 

787 #{lambda < -tol}: counting the <= variant at an arithmetically shifted 

788 threshold cannot be exact on the fp32 lattice (-tol*(1+2eps) lands 0, 2 

789 or 3 ULP below -tol depending on tol's mantissa, skipping representable 

790 eigenvalues), and a scalar bitcast nextafter miscompiles on this 

791 backend. The mirrored tie convention needs no shift at all and is 

792 exact for every tol, including 0 (#{lambda < 0}) and subnormals.""" 

793 q = tl.load(D + base) - x 

794 q = tl.where(q == 0.0, 1.1754944e-38, q) 

795 neg = (q < 0.0).to(tl.int32) 

796 i = 1 

797 while i < K: 

798 di = tl.load(D + base + i) 

799 ei = tl.load(E + base + i - 1) 

800 q = (di - x) - ei * ei / q 

801 q = tl.where(q == 0.0, 1.1754944e-38, q) 

802 neg += (q < 0.0).to(tl.int32) 

803 i += 1 

804 return neg 

805 

806 

807@triton.jit 

808def _sturm_count_posneg2(D, E, base, K: tl.constexpr, xp, xn): 

809 """Hermitian tolerance-bracket pair in ONE pass of the qd recurrence: 

810 chain 1 counts #{lambda <= xp} (DLANEG convention: zero pivot -> tiny 

811 NEGATIVE), chain 2 counts #{lambda < xn} STRICTLY (zero pivot -> tiny 

812 POSITIVE, see _sturm_count_strict). With xn = -tol the pair yields both 

813 sides of #{|lambda| > tol} = K - #{<= xp} + #{< xn} with exact tie 

814 semantics; pairing halves the serial K-step chain.""" 

815 d0 = tl.load(D + base) 

816 q1 = d0 - xp 

817 q2 = d0 - xn 

818 q1 = tl.where(q1 == 0.0, -1.1754944e-38, q1) 

819 q2 = tl.where(q2 == 0.0, 1.1754944e-38, q2) 

820 neg1 = (q1 < 0.0).to(tl.int32) 

821 neg2 = (q2 < 0.0).to(tl.int32) 

822 i = 1 

823 while i < K: 

824 di = tl.load(D + base + i) 

825 ei = tl.load(E + base + i - 1) 

826 e2 = ei * ei 

827 q1 = (di - xp) - e2 / q1 

828 q2 = (di - xn) - e2 / q2 

829 q1 = tl.where(q1 == 0.0, -1.1754944e-38, q1) 

830 q2 = tl.where(q2 == 0.0, 1.1754944e-38, q2) 

831 neg1 += (q1 < 0.0).to(tl.int32) 

832 neg2 += (q2 < 0.0).to(tl.int32) 

833 i += 1 

834 return neg1, neg2 

835 

836 

837@triton.jit 

838def _sturm_count_less_reg(dd, ee, K: tl.constexpr, BLOCK: tl.constexpr, x): 

839 """Register-resident variant of _sturm_count_less: identical qd 

840 recurrence and fp32 semantics, but the tridiagonal entries are extracted 

841 from register vectors with interval masks ((idx == i) is written as 

842 (idx > i-1) & (idx < i+1) -- an == mask on tl.arange miscompiles on this 

843 backend) instead of scalar global-memory loads. Used by the fused 

844 small-matrix kernels, where d/e never leave registers.""" 

845 kidx = tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

846 q = tl.sum(tl.where(kidx < 1, dd, 0.0), axis=0) - x 

847 q = tl.where(q == 0.0, -1.1754944e-38, q) 

848 neg = (q < 0.0).to(tl.int32) 

849 i = 1 

850 while i < K: 

851 di = tl.sum(tl.where((kidx > i - 1) & (kidx < i + 1), dd, 0.0), axis=0) 

852 ei = tl.sum(tl.where((kidx > i - 2) & (kidx < i), ee, 0.0), axis=0) 

853 q = (di - x) - ei * ei / q 

854 q = tl.where(q == 0.0, -1.1754944e-38, q) 

855 neg += (q < 0.0).to(tl.int32) 

856 i += 1 

857 return neg 

858 

859 

860@triton.jit 

861def _sturm_count_less_reg2(dd, ee, K: tl.constexpr, BLOCK: tl.constexpr, x1, x2): 

862 """Lockstep pair of _sturm_count_less_reg: two thresholds in ONE pass of 

863 the qd recurrence (the sequential K-step chain dominates the fused 

864 kernels' latency, and the hermitian bracket needs four counts -- pairing 

865 halves that). Identical fp32 semantics to two separate calls.""" 

866 kidx = tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

867 d0 = tl.sum(tl.where(kidx < 1, dd, 0.0), axis=0) 

868 q1 = d0 - x1 

869 q2 = d0 - x2 

870 q1 = tl.where(q1 == 0.0, -1.1754944e-38, q1) 

871 q2 = tl.where(q2 == 0.0, -1.1754944e-38, q2) 

872 neg1 = (q1 < 0.0).to(tl.int32) 

873 neg2 = (q2 < 0.0).to(tl.int32) 

874 i = 1 

875 while i < K: 

876 di = tl.sum(tl.where((kidx > i - 1) & (kidx < i + 1), dd, 0.0), axis=0) 

877 ei = tl.sum(tl.where((kidx > i - 2) & (kidx < i), ee, 0.0), axis=0) 

878 e2 = ei * ei 

879 q1 = (di - x1) - e2 / q1 

880 q2 = (di - x2) - e2 / q2 

881 q1 = tl.where(q1 == 0.0, -1.1754944e-38, q1) 

882 q2 = tl.where(q2 == 0.0, -1.1754944e-38, q2) 

883 neg1 += (q1 < 0.0).to(tl.int32) 

884 neg2 += (q2 < 0.0).to(tl.int32) 

885 i += 1 

886 return neg1, neg2 

887 

888 

889@triton.jit 

890def _sturm_count_strict_reg(dd, ee, K: tl.constexpr, BLOCK: tl.constexpr, x): 

891 """STRICT register-resident variant of _sturm_count_less_reg: counts 

892 #{lambda < x} via the mirrored zero-pivot tie convention (zero pivot -> 

893 tiny POSITIVE). See _sturm_count_strict for why this -- and not an 

894 arithmetically shifted threshold -- is the exact strict count.""" 

895 kidx = tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

896 q = tl.sum(tl.where(kidx < 1, dd, 0.0), axis=0) - x 

897 q = tl.where(q == 0.0, 1.1754944e-38, q) 

898 neg = (q < 0.0).to(tl.int32) 

899 i = 1 

900 while i < K: 

901 di = tl.sum(tl.where((kidx > i - 1) & (kidx < i + 1), dd, 0.0), axis=0) 

902 ei = tl.sum(tl.where((kidx > i - 2) & (kidx < i), ee, 0.0), axis=0) 

903 q = (di - x) - ei * ei / q 

904 q = tl.where(q == 0.0, 1.1754944e-38, q) 

905 neg += (q < 0.0).to(tl.int32) 

906 i += 1 

907 return neg 

908 

909 

910@triton.jit 

911def _sturm_count_posneg_reg2(dd, ee, K: tl.constexpr, BLOCK: tl.constexpr, xp, xn): 

912 """Register-resident counterpart of _sturm_count_posneg2: chain 1 counts 

913 #{lambda <= xp} (zero pivot -> tiny negative), chain 2 counts 

914 #{lambda < xn} STRICTLY (zero pivot -> tiny positive), in ONE pass of 

915 the qd recurrence over register-resident d/e vectors (interval masks -- 

916 an == mask on tl.arange miscompiles on this backend).""" 

917 kidx = tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

918 d0 = tl.sum(tl.where(kidx < 1, dd, 0.0), axis=0) 

919 q1 = d0 - xp 

920 q2 = d0 - xn 

921 q1 = tl.where(q1 == 0.0, -1.1754944e-38, q1) 

922 q2 = tl.where(q2 == 0.0, 1.1754944e-38, q2) 

923 neg1 = (q1 < 0.0).to(tl.int32) 

924 neg2 = (q2 < 0.0).to(tl.int32) 

925 i = 1 

926 while i < K: 

927 di = tl.sum(tl.where((kidx > i - 1) & (kidx < i + 1), dd, 0.0), axis=0) 

928 ei = tl.sum(tl.where((kidx > i - 2) & (kidx < i), ee, 0.0), axis=0) 

929 e2 = ei * ei 

930 q1 = (di - xp) - e2 / q1 

931 q2 = (di - xn) - e2 / q2 

932 q1 = tl.where(q1 == 0.0, -1.1754944e-38, q1) 

933 q2 = tl.where(q2 == 0.0, 1.1754944e-38, q2) 

934 neg1 += (q1 < 0.0).to(tl.int32) 

935 neg2 += (q2 < 0.0).to(tl.int32) 

936 i += 1 

937 return neg1, neg2

940@triton.jit 

941def _mr_sturm_rank_reg( 

942 dd, 

943 ee, 

944 d_raw, 

945 atol, 

946 rtol, 

947 K: tl.constexpr, 

948 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

949 HERMITIAN: tl.constexpr, 

950 BISECT_ITERS: tl.constexpr, 

951): 

952 """Rank from an in-register symmetric tridiagonal (dd, ee); d_raw is the 

953 pre-transform diagonal (raw bidiagonal d for the bidiag path, dd itself 

954 for the Gram path), used only by the HERMITIAN sigma_lo estimate. Exact 

955 register-resident counterpart of the logic that used to live in 

956 _matrix_rank_sturm_kernel: Gershgorin bounds, tolerance bracketing, and 

957 bisection on the Sturm count only when the rank depends on it.""" 

958 rows = tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

959 cols = tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

960 shift2d = (cols[None, :] > rows[:, None] - 2) & (cols[None, :] < rows[:, None]) 

961 e_prev_v = tl.sum(tl.where(shift2d, ee[None, :], 0.0), axis=1) 

962 gershgorin = tl.abs(dd) + tl.abs(ee) + tl.abs(e_prev_v) 

963 hi = tl.max(gershgorin, axis=0) 

964 dmax = tl.max(dd, axis=0) 

965 rank = tl.zeros((), dtype=tl.int32) 

966 if hi > 0.0: 

967 if HERMITIAN: 

968 # eigenvalues themselves; rank = #{lambda > tol} + #{lambda < -tol} 

969 sigma_lo = tl.maximum(tl.abs(dmax), tl.abs(tl.min(d_raw, axis=0))) 

970 tol_lo = tl.maximum(atol, rtol * sigma_lo) 

971 tol_hi = tl.maximum(atol, rtol * hi) 

972 cnt_lo_p, cnt_lo_n = _sturm_count_posneg_reg2( 

973 dd, ee, K, BLOCK, tol_lo, -tol_lo 

974 ) 

975 cnt_hi_p, cnt_hi_n = _sturm_count_posneg_reg2( 

976 dd, ee, K, BLOCK, tol_hi, -tol_hi 

977 ) 

978 rank_lo = (K - cnt_lo_p) + cnt_lo_n 

979 rank_hi = (K - cnt_hi_p) + cnt_hi_n 

980 rank = rank_lo 

981 refine = rank_lo != rank_hi 

982 if refine: 

983 # The rank depends on sigma_max: refine it by bisection. 

984 lo = dmax 

985 hi_p = hi * (1.0 + 1e-9) + 1e-30 

986 it = 0 

987 while it < BISECT_ITERS: 

988 mid = 0.5 * (lo + hi_p) 

989 cnt = _sturm_count_less_reg(dd, ee, K, BLOCK, mid) 

990 if cnt >= K: 

991 hi_p = mid 

992 else: 

993 lo = mid 

994 it += 1 

995 lmax = 0.5 * (lo + hi_p) 

996 lo = -(hi * (1.0 + 1e-9) + 1e-30) 

997 hi_p = tl.min(d_raw, axis=0) 

998 it = 0 

999 while it < BISECT_ITERS: 

1000 mid = 0.5 * (lo + hi_p) 

1001 cnt = _sturm_count_less_reg(dd, ee, K, BLOCK, mid) 

1002 if cnt > 0: 

1003 hi_p = mid 

1004 else: 

1005 lo = mid 

1006 it += 1 

1007 lmin = 0.5 * (lo + hi_p) 

1008 sigma_max = tl.maximum(tl.abs(lmax), tl.abs(lmin)) 

1009 tol = tl.maximum(atol, rtol * sigma_max) 

1010 rank = (K - _sturm_count_less_reg(dd, ee, K, BLOCK, tol)) + ( 

1011 _sturm_count_strict_reg(dd, ee, K, BLOCK, -tol) 

1012 ) 

1013 else: 

1014 # Gram matrix: eigenvalues are sigma^2, threshold is tol^2. 

1015 sigma_lo = tl.sqrt(tl.maximum(dmax, 0.0)) 

1016 sigma_hi = tl.sqrt(hi) 

1017 tol_lo = tl.maximum(atol, rtol * sigma_lo) 

1018 tol_hi = tl.maximum(atol, rtol * sigma_hi) 

1019 cnt_lo, cnt_hi = _sturm_count_less_reg2( 

1020 dd, ee, K, BLOCK, tol_lo * tol_lo, tol_hi * tol_hi 

1021 ) 

1022 rank = K - cnt_lo 

1023 refine = rank != (K - cnt_hi) 

1024 if refine: 

1025 # The rank depends on sigma_max: refine it by bisection. 

1026 lo = tl.maximum(dmax, 0.0) 

1027 hi_p = hi * (1.0 + 1e-9) + 1e-30 

1028 it = 0 

1029 while it < BISECT_ITERS: 

1030 mid = 0.5 * (lo + hi_p) 

1031 cnt = _sturm_count_less_reg(dd, ee, K, BLOCK, mid) 

1032 if cnt >= K: 

1033 hi_p = mid 

1034 else: 

1035 lo = mid 

1036 it += 1 

1037 lmax = 0.5 * (lo + hi_p) 

1038 sigma_max = tl.sqrt(lmax) 

1039 tol = tl.maximum(atol, rtol * sigma_max) 

1040 rank = K - _sturm_count_less_reg(dd, ee, K, BLOCK, tol * tol) 

1041 return rank 

1042 

1043 

1044@libentry() 

1045@triton.jit 

1046def _matrix_rank_gram_kernel( 

1047 A, 

1048 G, 

1049 PM: tl.constexpr, 

1050 PN: tl.constexpr, 

1051 TALL: tl.constexpr, 

1052 BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr, 

1053): 

1054 """G[b] = A[b]^T A[b] (tall) or A[b] A[b]^T (wide) on the Cube. 

1055 

1056 Fast opt-in path (FLAGGEMS_MR_FAST_PATH=1) for long-dimension inputs 

1057 (one of m, n > 64), k <= 64: fast, but the sigma^2-domain floor 

1058 overestimates rank on slowly-decaying spectra -- the default dispatch 

1059 routes these inputs to the exact QR-compression path instead. Input 

1060 is pre-padded 

1061 by the launcher to (PM, PN) multiples of 32 with the short dimension 

1062 64, so every tl.dot operand is a full unpadded block. The accumulator 

1063 is summed in plain vector adds (the dot-accumulator form loses 

1064 precision), and the transposed operand is a normal load run through 

1065 tl.trans (stride-swapped loads fed to tl.dot miscompile). 

1066 """ 

1067 batch = tl.program_id(0) 

1068 a_base = A + batch * PM * PN 

1069 rows = tl.arange(0, 64) 

1070 cols = tl.arange(0, 64) 

1071 g = tl.zeros((64, 64), dtype=tl.float32) 

1072 if TALL: 

1073 for m0 in tl.static_range(0, PM, BLOCK_M): 

1074 mr = m0 + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_M) 

1075 b = tl.load(a_base + mr[:, None] * PN + cols[None, :]) 

1076 g = g + tl.dot(tl.trans(b), b, input_precision="ieee") 

1077 else: 

1078 for n0 in tl.static_range(0, PN, BLOCK_M): 

1079 mc = n0 + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_M) 

1080 at = tl.load(a_base + rows[:, None] * PN + mc[None, :]) 

1081 g = g + tl.dot(at, tl.trans(at), input_precision="ieee") 

1082 tl.store(G + batch * 64 * 64 + rows[:, None] * 64 + cols[None, :], g) 

1083 

1084 

1085@libentry() 

1086@triton.jit 

1087def _matrix_rank_tridiag_kernel( 

1088 A, 

1089 D, 

1090 E, 

1091 K: tl.constexpr, 

1092 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

1093): 

1094 # Householder tridiagonalization of the host-presymmetrized padded 

1095 # hermitian input (33..64 band). The symmetrization itself stays on 

1096 # the host: both a 64x64 computed-address gather (~90us) and a 

1097 # tl.trans + select of the tile (~68us) cost far more inside this 

1098 # kernel than the aten equivalent (~7us). Rank-2 trailing update as 

1099 # one reshape outer product. 

1100 batch = tl.program_id(0) 

1101 rows = tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

1102 cols = tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

1103 g = tl.load(A + batch * BLOCK * BLOCK + rows[:, None] * BLOCK + cols[None, :]) 

1104 d_vec = tl.zeros((BLOCK,), dtype=tl.float32) 

1105 e_vec = tl.zeros((BLOCK,), dtype=tl.float32) 

1106 for j in tl.range(0, K - 1): 

1107 colmask = (cols[None, :] > j - 1) & (cols[None, :] < j + 1) 

1108 v_vec = tl.sum(tl.where(colmask, g, 0.0), axis=1) 

1109 m0 = (rows > j) & (rows < j + 2) 

1110 x0 = tl.sum(v_vec * m0.to(tl.float32), axis=0) 

1111 v = v_vec * (rows > j).to(tl.float32) 

1112 sigma = tl.sqrt(tl.sum(v * v, axis=0)) 

1113 alpha = tl.where(x0 >= 0.0, -sigma, sigma) 

1114 v2 = tl.where(m0, x0 - alpha, v) 

1115 vnorm2 = 2.0 * sigma * (sigma + tl.abs(x0)) 

1116 tau = tl.where(vnorm2 > 0.0, 2.0 / vnorm2, 0.0) 

1117 w = tau * tl.sum(g * v2[None, :], axis=1) 

1118 beta = -0.5 * tau * tl.sum(v2 * w, axis=0) 

1119 w2 = (w + beta * v2) * (cols > j).to(tl.float32) 

1120 upd = tl.reshape(v2, (BLOCK, 1)) * tl.reshape(w2, (1, BLOCK)) 

1121 updt = tl.reshape(w2, (BLOCK, 1)) * tl.reshape(v2, (1, BLOCK)) 

1122 g = g - upd - updt 

1123 dmask = ((rows > j - 1) & (rows < j + 1)).to(tl.float32) 

1124 d_vec = d_vec + v_vec * dmask 

1125 e_vec = e_vec + alpha * dmask 

1126 vlast = tl.sum( 

1127 tl.where((cols[None, :] > K - 2) & (cols[None, :] < K), g, 0.0), axis=1 

1128 ) 

1129 d_vec = d_vec + vlast * ((rows > K - 2) & (rows < K)).to(tl.float32) 

1130 # NOTE: the store carries the batch offset (the pre-fusion version wrote 

1131 # every program's d/e to batch 0's slot, corrupting batched inputs). 

1132 tl.store(D + batch * BLOCK + rows, d_vec) 

1133 tl.store(E + batch * BLOCK + rows, e_vec) 

1134 

1135 

1136@libentry() 

1137@triton.jit 

1138def _matrix_rank_small_fused_kernel( 

1139 A, 

1140 ATOL, 

1141 RTOL, 

1142 OUT, 

1143 ATOL_VAL, 

1144 RTOL_VAL, 

1145 M: tl.constexpr, 

1146 N: tl.constexpr, 

1147 K: tl.constexpr, 

1148 HERMITIAN: tl.constexpr, 

1149 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

1150 BISECT_ITERS: tl.constexpr, 

1151 TOL_TENSOR: tl.constexpr, 

1152): 

1153 # Fused small-matrix path (M, N <= 32): reduction + Sturm rank count in 

1154 # ONE kernel launch (this fusion removes two kernel launches, the padded 

1155 # staging buffer, and the d/e global-memory round trip, which dominated 

1156 # the wall-clock latency of small matrices). One program per matrix. 

1157 # The input tile is loaded directly with a zero-filling bounds mask -- 

1158 # no tl.dot is fed by this load, so the masked-operand miscompile that 

1159 # forces padding on the Gram path does not apply here. 

1160 # 

1161 # Non-hermitian: Golub-Kahan bidiagonalization (the exact math of the 

1162 # former _matrix_rank_bidiag_kernel: two-sided Householder reflections 

1163 # via reshape-based outer products, axis-1 masked reductions, and 

1164 # strict-inequality interval masks), then the B^T B tridiagonal entries 

1165 # are constructed exactly from the bidiagonal d/e (d_i^2 + e_{i-1}^2 and 

1166 # d_i e_i), so the smallest singular value keeps LINEAR precision. 

1167 # 

1168 # Hermitian: one-sided Householder TRIDIAGONALIZATION of A directly -- 

1169 # half the reflections of the bidiagonalization and no tl.trans, and the 

1170 # Sturm count runs on the tridiagonal in the eigenvalue domain (no 

1171 # squaring), which is both faster and more accurate for symmetric input. 

1172 batch = tl.program_id(0) 

1173 rows = tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

1174 cols = tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

1175 if not HERMITIAN and M < N: 

1176 # Wide input: bidiagonalize A^T instead (sigma(A^T) == sigma(A)), 

1177 # so the reduction below always works on the tall form -- the GK 

1178 # loop needs K left reflections for the tall form (a K-1 loop plus 

1179 # a diagonal readout loses the column K-1 tail energy of tall 

1180 # inputs and the row K-1 tail of wide ones). A strided transposed 

1181 # load is ~10x slower than a normal load + register trans on this 

1182 # backend, hence the trans. M, N, HERMITIAN are constexpr, so 

1183 # square/tall inputs compile to the plain load. 

1184 g0 = tl.load( 

1185 A + batch * M * N + rows[:, None] * N + cols[None, :], 

1186 mask=(rows[:, None] < M) & (cols[None, :] < N), 

1187 other=0.0, 

1188 ) 

1189 g = tl.trans(g0) 

1190 else: 

1191 lmask = (rows[:, None] < M) & (cols[None, :] < N) 

1192 g = tl.load( 

1193 A + batch * M * N + rows[:, None] * N + cols[None, :], mask=lmask, other=0.0 

1194 ) 

1195 if HERMITIAN: 

1196 # torch hermitian semantics: only the LOWER triangle of A may be 

1197 # used; rebuild the strict upper triangle from the lower one in 

1198 # registers (a garbage upper triangle must not leak into the 

1199 # tridiagonalization). 

1200 g = tl.where(rows[:, None] >= cols[None, :], g, tl.trans(g)) 

1201 d_vec = tl.zeros((BLOCK,), dtype=tl.float32) 

1202 e_vec = tl.zeros((BLOCK,), dtype=tl.float32) 

1203 if HERMITIAN: 

1204 # One-sided Householder tridiagonalization (the math of 

1205 # _matrix_rank_tridiag_kernel): rank-2 trailing update as one 

1206 # reshape outer product. 

1207 for j in tl.range(0, K - 1): 

1208 colmask = (cols[None, :] > j - 1) & (cols[None, :] < j + 1) 

1209 v_vec = tl.sum(tl.where(colmask, g, 0.0), axis=1) 

1210 m0 = (rows > j) & (rows < j + 2) 

1211 x0 = tl.sum(v_vec * m0.to(tl.float32), axis=0) 

1212 v = v_vec * (rows > j).to(tl.float32) 

1213 sigma = tl.sqrt(tl.sum(v * v, axis=0)) 

1214 alpha = tl.where(x0 >= 0.0, -sigma, sigma) 

1215 v2 = tl.where(m0, x0 - alpha, v) 

1216 vnorm2 = 2.0 * sigma * (sigma + tl.abs(x0)) 

1217 tau = tl.where(vnorm2 > 0.0, 2.0 / vnorm2, 0.0) 

1218 w = tau * tl.sum(g * v2[None, :], axis=1) 

1219 beta = -0.5 * tau * tl.sum(v2 * w, axis=0) 

1220 w2 = (w + beta * v2) * (cols > j).to(tl.float32) 

1221 upd = tl.reshape(v2, (BLOCK, 1)) * tl.reshape(w2, (1, BLOCK)) 

1222 updt = tl.reshape(w2, (BLOCK, 1)) * tl.reshape(v2, (1, BLOCK)) 

1223 g = g - upd - updt 

1224 dmask = ((rows > j - 1) & (rows < j + 1)).to(tl.float32) 

1225 d_vec = d_vec + v_vec * dmask 

1226 e_vec = e_vec + alpha * dmask 

1227 vlast = tl.sum( 

1228 tl.where((cols[None, :] > K - 2) & (cols[None, :] < K), g, 0.0), axis=1 

1229 ) 

1230 d_vec = d_vec + vlast * ((rows > K - 2) & (rows < K)).to(tl.float32) 

1231 # eigenvalue-domain tridiagonal: feed the Sturm count directly. 

1232 dd = d_vec 

1233 ee = e_vec 

1234 else: 

1235 gT = tl.trans(g) 

1236 # K left reflections (the tall form needs the last one: it folds 

1237 # the column K-1 tail into d[K-1]); the right reflection is 

1238 # inert at j = K-1 (u == 0 there) and skipped when j + 2 >= K. 

1239 for j in tl.range(0, K): 

1240 # ---- left reflection: zero g[j+1:, j] ---- 

1241 colmask = (cols[None, :] > j - 1) & (cols[None, :] < j + 1) 

1242 colj = tl.sum(tl.where(colmask, g, 0.0), axis=1) 

1243 x0 = tl.sum(colj * ((rows > j - 1) & (rows < j + 1)).to(tl.float32), axis=0) 

1244 x = colj * (rows >= j).to(tl.float32) 

1245 sigma = tl.sqrt(tl.sum(x * x, axis=0)) 

1246 alpha = tl.where(x0 >= 0.0, -sigma, sigma) 

1247 v2 = tl.where((rows > j - 1) & (rows < j + 1), x0 - alpha, x) 

1248 vnorm2 = 2.0 * sigma * (sigma + tl.abs(x0)) 

1249 tau = tl.where(vnorm2 > 0.0, 2.0 / vnorm2, 0.0) 

1250 # w = tau * (g[j:, :]^T v2) via gT (axis-1 reduce, stable) 

1251 w = tau * tl.sum(gT * v2[None, :], axis=1) 

1252 g = g - tl.reshape(v2, (BLOCK, 1)) * tl.reshape(w, (1, BLOCK)) 

1253 gT = tl.trans(g) 

1254 # D[j] = alpha: the left reflection maps g[j, j] to +/-sigma 

1255 d_vec = d_vec + alpha * ((rows > j - 1) & (rows < j + 1)).to(tl.float32) 

1256 # ---- right reflection: zero g[j, j+2:] ---- 

1257 rowmask = (rows[None, :] > j - 1) & (rows[None, :] < j + 1) 

1258 rowj = tl.sum(tl.where(rowmask, gT, 0.0), axis=0) 

1259 u0 = tl.sum(rowj * ((cols > j) & (cols < j + 2)).to(tl.float32), axis=0) 

1260 u = rowj * (cols > j).to(tl.float32) 

1261 sigma2 = tl.sqrt(tl.sum(u * u, axis=0)) 

1262 alpha2 = tl.where(u0 >= 0.0, -sigma2, sigma2) 

1263 if j + 2 < K: 

1264 u2 = tl.where((cols > j) & (cols < j + 2), u0 - alpha2, u) 

1265 vnorm3 = 2.0 * sigma2 * (sigma2 + tl.abs(u0)) 

1266 tau2 = tl.where(vnorm3 > 0.0, 2.0 / vnorm3, 0.0) 

1267 # z = tau2 * (g[:, j+1:] u2): axis-1 reduce 

1268 z = tau2 * tl.sum(g * u2[None, :], axis=1) 

1269 g = g - tl.reshape(z, (BLOCK, 1)) * tl.reshape(u2, (1, BLOCK)) 

1270 gT = tl.trans(g) 

1271 if j + 1 < K: 

1272 # E[j] = alpha2: the right reflection maps g[j, j+1] to +/-sigma 

1273 e_vec = e_vec + alpha2 * ((rows > j - 1) & (rows < j + 1)).to( 

1274 tl.float32 

1275 ) 

1276 # B^T B tridiagonal entries, exact from the bidiagonal d/e: 

1277 # dd_i = d_i^2 + e_{i-1}^2, ee_i = d_i * e_i. 

1278 shift2d = (cols[None, :] > rows[:, None] - 2) & (cols[None, :] < rows[:, None]) 

1279 e_prev = tl.sum(tl.where(shift2d, e_vec[None, :], 0.0), axis=1) 

1280 dd = d_vec * d_vec + e_prev * e_prev 

1281 ee = d_vec * e_vec 

1282 if TOL_TENSOR: 

1283 atol = tl.load(ATOL + batch) 

1284 rtol = tl.load(RTOL + batch) 

1285 else: 

1286 atol = ATOL_VAL 

1287 rtol = RTOL_VAL 

1288 rank = _mr_sturm_rank_reg( 

1289 dd, ee, d_vec, atol, rtol, K, BLOCK, HERMITIAN, BISECT_ITERS 

1290 ) 

1291 tl.store(OUT + batch, rank.to(tl.int64)) 

1292 

1293 

1294@triton.jit 

1295def _matrix_rank_bidiag64_kernel( 

1296 A, D, E, M, N, K, BLOCK: tl.constexpr 

1297): # One program per matrix: Golub-Kahan bidiagonalization for the 

1298 # non-hermitian 32 < k <= 64 band (m, n <= 64), writing the RAW 

1299 # bidiagonal d/e to global memory (the Sturm tail -- to_tridiag / 

1300 # sturm_big / sturm_final -- is shared with the large-matrix path). 

1301 # 

1302 # Structural choices vs the deleted _matrix_rank_bidiag_kernel, all 

1303 # aimed at the BLOCK=64 miscompile cluster (report, stage 5): 

1304 # * M, N, K are RUNTIME values: one compilation covers the whole band 

1305 # instead of one miscompile lottery ticket per K. 

1306 # * the input is loaded directly with a zero-filling bounds mask (no 

1307 # padded staging buffer, no unmasked load). 

1308 # * no tl.trans inside the loop: gT is maintained incrementally with 

1309 # the transposed outer product of each update (the 64x64 trans slow 

1310 # path measured ~68us in this kernel class). 

1311 # * the last-step right-reflector skip is done by zeroing tau2 with a 

1312 # float mask, not an scf.if around tile ops. E is still recorded 

1313 # (its magnitude is |u0| either way; per-element sign flips of the 

1314 # bidiagonal are diagonal +-1 similarities and do not change the 

1315 # singular values being counted). 

1316 batch = tl.program_id(0) 

1317 rows = tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

1318 cols = tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

1319 # Wide inputs (M < N) are bidiagonalized TRANSPOSED: sigma(A^T) == 

1320 # sigma(A) and the tall form keeps the reduction uniform (the B^T B 

1321 # construction in the Sturm tail assumes the tall/square bidiagonal 

1322 # layout). A strided transposed LOAD is ~10x slower than a normal 

1323 # load + register trans on this backend, and an scf.if around the tile 

1324 # load is a miscompile risk, so: load normally, take one register 

1325 # trans, and select with a scalar-conditioned where. 

1326 lmask = (rows[:, None] < M) & (cols[None, :] < N) 

1327 g0 = tl.load( 

1328 A + batch * M * N + rows[:, None] * N + cols[None, :], mask=lmask, other=0.0 

1329 ) 

1330 gT0 = tl.trans(g0) 

1331 wide = M < N 

1332 g = tl.where(wide, gT0, g0) 

1333 gT = tl.where(wide, g0, gT0) 

1334 d_vec = tl.zeros((BLOCK,), dtype=tl.float32) 

1335 e_vec = tl.zeros((BLOCK,), dtype=tl.float32) 

1336 for j in tl.range(0, K): 

1337 # ---- left reflection: zero g[j+1:, j] ---- 

1338 colmask = (cols[None, :] > j - 1) & (cols[None, :] < j + 1) 

1339 colj = tl.sum(tl.where(colmask, g, 0.0), axis=1) 

1340 x0 = tl.sum(colj * ((rows > j - 1) & (rows < j + 1)).to(tl.float32), axis=0) 

1341 x = colj * (rows >= j).to(tl.float32) 

1342 sigma = tl.sqrt(tl.sum(x * x, axis=0)) 

1343 alpha = tl.where(x0 >= 0.0, -sigma, sigma) 

1344 v2 = tl.where((rows > j - 1) & (rows < j + 1), x0 - alpha, x) 

1345 vnorm2 = 2.0 * sigma * (sigma + tl.abs(x0)) 

1346 tau = tl.where(vnorm2 > 0.0, 2.0 / vnorm2, 0.0) 

1347 # w = tau * (g^T v2); update g and the incrementally maintained gT 

1348 w = tau * tl.sum(gT * v2[None, :], axis=1) 

1349 g = g - tl.reshape(v2, (BLOCK, 1)) * tl.reshape(w, (1, BLOCK)) 

1350 gT = gT - tl.reshape(w, (BLOCK, 1)) * tl.reshape(v2, (1, BLOCK)) 

1351 # D[j] = alpha: the left reflection maps g[j, j] to +/-sigma 

1352 d_vec = d_vec + alpha * ((rows > j - 1) & (rows < j + 1)).to(tl.float32) 

1353 # ---- right reflection: zero g[j, j+2:] ---- 

1354 coljT = (cols[None, :] > j - 1) & (cols[None, :] < j + 1) 

1355 rowj = tl.sum(tl.where(coljT, gT, 0.0), axis=1) 

1356 u0 = tl.sum(rowj * ((cols > j) & (cols < j + 2)).to(tl.float32), axis=0) 

1357 u = rowj * (cols > j).to(tl.float32) 

1358 sigma2 = tl.sqrt(tl.sum(u * u, axis=0)) 

1359 alpha2 = tl.where(u0 >= 0.0, -sigma2, sigma2) 

1360 u2 = tl.where((cols > j) & (cols < j + 2), u0 - alpha2, u) 

1361 vnorm3 = 2.0 * sigma2 * (sigma2 + tl.abs(u0)) 

1362 # gate the reflector off once row j has <= 2 in-range elements 

1363 # (j + 2 >= K, nothing to zero) by zeroing tau2 -- no scf.if around 

1364 # the tile ops. At j == K-1 u is identically zero, which also 

1365 # makes this a no-op for the tall last step. 

1366 tau2 = tl.where(vnorm3 > 0.0, 2.0 / vnorm3, 0.0) * (j + 2 < K).to(tl.float32) 

1367 z = tau2 * tl.sum(g * u2[None, :], axis=1) 

1368 g = g - tl.reshape(z, (BLOCK, 1)) * tl.reshape(u2, (1, BLOCK)) 

1369 gT = gT - tl.reshape(u2, (BLOCK, 1)) * tl.reshape(z, (1, BLOCK)) 

1370 # E[j] = alpha2 (magnitude is right even when the reflector is 

1371 # gated off: |alpha2| == |g[j, j+1]|). 

1372 e_vec = e_vec + alpha2 * ((rows > j - 1) & (rows < j + 1)).to(tl.float32) 

1373 tl.store(D + batch * K + rows, d_vec, mask=rows < K) 

1374 tl.store(E + batch * K + rows, e_vec, mask=rows < K) 

1375 

1376 

1377@triton.jit 

1378def _mr_extract_upper_kernel(W, PIV, RB, K, RS, WPITCH, BLOCK: tl.constexpr): 

1379 # Extract the upper-triangular R (K x K, row-major) from the QR work 

1380 # matrix W (column-major tiles, row pitch RS). Convention of the panel 

1381 # kernels: W holds R STRICTLY above the diagonal (the diagonal itself is 

1382 # stale -- R[j, j] = PIV[j], the reflection alpha) and reflector 

1383 # sideband data below it. 

1384 pid = tl.program_id(0) 

1385 lr = tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

1386 lc = tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

1387 tile = tl.load( 

1388 W + pid * WPITCH + lc[:, None] * RS + lr[None, :], 

1389 mask=(lc[:, None] < K) & (lr[None, :] < lc[:, None]), 

1390 other=0.0, 

1391 ) 

1392 piv = tl.load(PIV + pid * K + lc, mask=lc < K, other=0.0) 

1393 tile = tile + piv[:, None] * ( 

1394 (lr[None, :] > lc[:, None] - 1) & (lr[None, :] < lc[:, None] + 1) 

1395 ).to(tl.float32) 

1396 # tile[c, r] = R[r, c]; scatter to row-major RB[r*K + c] 

1397 tl.store( 

1398 RB + pid * K * K + lr[None, :] * K + lc[:, None], 

1399 tile, 

1400 mask=(lc[:, None] < K) & (lr[None, :] < K), 

1401 ) 

1402 

1403 

1404@libentry() 

1405@triton.jit 

1406def _matrix_rank_sturm_kernel( 

1407 D, 

1408 E, 

1409 ATOL, 

1410 RTOL, 

1411 OUT, 

1412 ATOL_VAL, 

1413 RTOL_VAL, 

1414 K: tl.constexpr, 

1415 HERMITIAN: tl.constexpr, 

1416 BIDIAG: tl.constexpr, 

1417 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

1418 BISECT_ITERS: tl.constexpr, 

1419 TOL_TENSOR: tl.constexpr, 

1420): 

1421 # Rank of a symmetric tridiagonal (B^T B of a Gram matrix, or the 

1422 # direct tridiagonalization output), using Gershgorin bounds refined 

1423 # by bisection on the Sturm count only when the rank actually depends 

1424 # on the refinement. One program per batch element; D/E were produced 

1425 # in a PREVIOUS launch, so this kernel only reads global memory 

1426 # (kernel boundaries serialize the MTE3/MTE2 queues). D/E always hold 

1427 # the FINAL tridiagonal on entry, so BIDIAG is False at every call 

1428 # site (the True branch is a legacy dead switch kept to preserve the 

1429 # verified compilation of this kernel) and the store-back below 

1430 # re-writes identical values (idempotent): no result depends on 

1431 # same-kernel store->load ordering, which is NOT guaranteed on this 

1432 # backend. 

1433 batch = tl.program_id(0) 

1434 kidx = tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

1435 rows = tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

1436 cols = tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

1437 base = batch * BLOCK 

1438 d = tl.load(D + base + kidx, mask=kidx < K, other=0.0) 

1439 e_cur = tl.load(E + base + kidx, mask=kidx < K - 1, other=0.0) 

1440 e_prev = tl.load(E + base + kidx - 1, mask=(kidx >= 1) & (kidx < K), other=0.0) 

1441 if BIDIAG: 

1442 dd = d * d + e_prev * e_prev 

1443 ee = d * e_cur 

1444 else: 

1445 dd = d 

1446 ee = e_cur 

1447 tl.store(D + base + kidx, dd, mask=kidx < K) 

1448 tl.store(E + base + kidx, ee, mask=kidx < K) 

1449 shift2d = (cols[None, :] > rows[:, None] - 2) & (cols[None, :] < rows[:, None]) 

1450 e_prev_v = tl.sum(tl.where(shift2d, ee[None, :], 0.0), axis=1) 

1451 gershgorin = tl.abs(dd) + tl.abs(ee) + tl.abs(e_prev_v) 

1452 hi = tl.max(gershgorin, axis=0) 

1453 dmax = tl.max(dd, axis=0) 

1454 if TOL_TENSOR: 

1455 atol = tl.load(ATOL + batch) 

1456 rtol = tl.load(RTOL + batch) 

1457 else: 

1458 atol = ATOL_VAL 

1459 rtol = RTOL_VAL 

1460 

1461 if hi == 0.0: 

1462 # The tridiagonal (and hence the matrix) is exactly zero. 

1463 tl.store(OUT + batch, tl.zeros((), dtype=tl.int64)) 

1464 else: 

1465 if HERMITIAN: 

1466 # eigenvalues themselves; rank = #{lambda > tol} + #{lambda < -tol} 

1467 sigma_lo = tl.maximum(tl.abs(dmax), tl.abs(tl.min(d, axis=0))) 

1468 tol_lo = tl.maximum(atol, rtol * sigma_lo) 

1469 tol_hi = tl.maximum(atol, rtol * hi) 

1470 cnt_lo_p, cnt_lo_n = _sturm_count_posneg2(D, E, base, K, tol_lo, -tol_lo) 

1471 cnt_hi_p, cnt_hi_n = _sturm_count_posneg2(D, E, base, K, tol_hi, -tol_hi) 

1472 rank_lo = (K - cnt_lo_p) + cnt_lo_n 

1473 rank_hi = (K - cnt_hi_p) + cnt_hi_n 

1474 else: 

1475 # Gram matrix: eigenvalues are sigma^2, threshold is tol^2. 

1476 sigma_lo = tl.sqrt(tl.maximum(dmax, 0.0)) 

1477 sigma_hi = tl.sqrt(hi) 

1478 tol_lo = tl.maximum(atol, rtol * sigma_lo) 

1479 tol_hi = tl.maximum(atol, rtol * sigma_hi) 

1480 cnt_lo, cnt_hi = _sturm_count_less2( 

1481 D, E, base, K, tol_lo * tol_lo, tol_hi * tol_hi 

1482 ) 

1483 rank_lo = K - cnt_lo 

1484 rank_hi = K - cnt_hi 

1485 rank = rank_lo 

1486 refine = rank_lo != rank_hi 

1487 if refine: 

1488 # The rank depends on sigma_max: refine it by bisection. 

1489 if HERMITIAN: 

1490 lo = dmax 

1491 hi_p = hi * (1.0 + 1e-9) + 1e-30 

1492 it = 0 

1493 while it < BISECT_ITERS: 

1494 mid = 0.5 * (lo + hi_p) 

1495 cnt = _sturm_count_less(D, E, base, K, mid) 

1496 if cnt >= K: 

1497 hi_p = mid 

1498 else: 

1499 lo = mid 

1500 it += 1 

1501 lmax = 0.5 * (lo + hi_p) 

1502 lo = -(hi * (1.0 + 1e-9) + 1e-30) 

1503 hi_p = tl.min(d, axis=0) 

1504 it = 0 

1505 while it < BISECT_ITERS: 

1506 mid = 0.5 * (lo + hi_p) 

1507 cnt = _sturm_count_less(D, E, base, K, mid) 

1508 if cnt > 0: 

1509 hi_p = mid 

1510 else: 

1511 lo = mid 

1512 it += 1 

1513 lmin = 0.5 * (lo + hi_p) 

1514 sigma_max = tl.maximum(tl.abs(lmax), tl.abs(lmin)) 

1515 tol = tl.maximum(atol, rtol * sigma_max) 

1516 rank = (K - _sturm_count_less(D, E, base, K, tol)) + ( 

1517 _sturm_count_strict(D, E, base, K, -tol) 

1518 ) 

1519 else: 

1520 lo = tl.maximum(dmax, 0.0) 

1521 hi_p = hi * (1.0 + 1e-9) + 1e-30 

1522 it = 0 

1523 while it < BISECT_ITERS: 

1524 mid = 0.5 * (lo + hi_p) 

1525 cnt = _sturm_count_less(D, E, base, K, mid) 

1526 if cnt >= K: 

1527 hi_p = mid 

1528 else: 

1529 lo = mid 

1530 it += 1 

1531 lmax = 0.5 * (lo + hi_p) 

1532 sigma_max = tl.sqrt(lmax) 

1533 tol = tl.maximum(atol, rtol * sigma_max) 

1534 rank = K - _sturm_count_less(D, E, base, K, tol * tol) 

1535 tl.store(OUT + batch, rank.to(tl.int64)) 

1536 

1537 

1538_HERMITIAN_LOWER_MASK_CACHE = {} 

1539 

1540 

1541def _hermitian_lower_mask(m, n, device): 

1542 """Broadcastable (m, n) bool mask of the lower triangle (diagonal 

1543 included), cached per shape/device -- building it every call would cost 

1544 more than the single aten ``where`` it feeds.""" 

1545 key = (m, n, str(device)) 

1546 mask = _HERMITIAN_LOWER_MASK_CACHE.get(key) 

1547 if mask is None: 

1548 rows = torch.arange(m, device=device).unsqueeze(1) 

1549 cols = torch.arange(n, device=device).unsqueeze(0) 

1550 mask = rows >= cols 

1551 _HERMITIAN_LOWER_MASK_CACHE[key] = mask 

1552 return mask 

1553 

1554 

1555def _launch_tridiag_rank( 

1556 matrix, 

1557 atol_tensor, 

1558 rtol_tensor, 

1559 atol_val, 

1560 rtol_val, 

1561 out, 

1562 m, 

1563 n, 

1564 batch_count, 

1565 input, 

1566 hermitian, 

1567): 

1568 """Small/medium paths for k <= 64, fp32. 

1569 

1570 Small tiles (m, n <= 32) go to _matrix_rank_small_fused_kernel 

1571 (bidiagonalization + Sturm count in one launch, direct masked load of 

1572 A -- no padding); hermitian 32 < k <= 64 uses the padded 

1573 tridiagonalization + Sturm kernels (the fused variant miscompiles at 

1574 BLOCK = 64); non-hermitian 32 < k <= 64 with m, n <= 64 goes to 

1575 _matrix_rank_bidiag64_kernel + the shared Sturm tail; long-dimension 

1576 inputs go to _launch_longdim_rank (QR-compress to the k x k R factor, 

1577 then the same exact tail). 

1578 When atol/rtol are plain scalars they are passed as kernel scalar 

1579 arguments (TOL_TENSOR=False) and the tolerance tensors are never 

1580 materialized; ATOL/RTOL then receive a dummy pointer that is never 

1581 dereferenced. 

1582 """ 

1583 k = min(m, n) 

1584 rows = max(m, n) 

1585 block_m = 32 

1586 tol_tensor = atol_tensor is not None 

1587 if tol_tensor: 

1588 at_arg = atol_tensor 

1589 rt_arg = rtol_tensor 

1590 else: 

1591 at_arg = matrix 

1592 rt_arg = matrix 

1593 with torch_device_fn.device(input.device): 

1594 small = m <= 64 and n <= 64 

1595 # tile size adapts to the matrix: 32-wide tiles are cheaper and 

1596 # are correct on this backend (verified for K <= 32) 

1597 block = max(triton.next_power_of_2(max(m, n)), 32) if small else 64 

1598 if small and block <= 32: 

1599 # Single fused launch (verified correct on this backend only 

1600 # for BLOCK <= 32; at BLOCK = 64 the fused kernel miscompiles 

1601 # for many K). 

1602 _matrix_rank_small_fused_kernel[(batch_count,)]( 

1603 matrix, 

1604 at_arg, 

1605 rt_arg, 

1606 out, 

1607 atol_val, 

1608 rtol_val, 

1609 M=m, 

1610 N=n, 

1611 K=k, 

1612 HERMITIAN=hermitian, 

1613 BLOCK=block, 

1614 BISECT_ITERS=32, 

1615 TOL_TENSOR=tol_tensor, 

1616 num_warps=4, 

1617 num_stages=1, 

1618 enable_fp_fusion=True, 

1619 ) 

1620 elif small and hermitian: 

1621 # 32 < k <= 64 hermitian: one-sided Householder 

1622 # tridiagonalization of the zero-padded input -- half the 

1623 # reflections of the bidiagonalization, and the Sturm count 

1624 # runs in the eigenvalue domain directly (faster and more 

1625 # accurate for symmetric input). torch's lower-triangle-only 

1626 # hermitian semantics are enforced on the HOST while filling 

1627 # the padding (one cached-mask aten where, ~7us incremental 

1628 # over the plain copy; doing it inside the kernel costs ~68us 

1629 # at BLOCK=64, measured). 

1630 padded = torch.zeros( 

1631 (batch_count, block, block), 

1632 dtype=torch.float32, 

1633 device=input.device, 

1634 ) 

1635 torch.where( 

1636 _hermitian_lower_mask(m, n, matrix.device), 

1637 matrix, 

1638 matrix.mT, 

1639 out=padded[:, :m, :n], 

1640 ) 

1641 d = torch.empty( 

1642 (batch_count, block), dtype=torch.float32, device=input.device 

1643 ) 

1644 e = torch.empty( 

1645 (batch_count, block), dtype=torch.float32, device=input.device 

1646 ) 

1647 _matrix_rank_tridiag_kernel[(batch_count,)]( 

1648 padded, 

1649 d, 

1650 e, 

1651 K=k, 

1652 BLOCK=block, 

1653 num_warps=4, 

1654 num_stages=1, 

1655 enable_fp_fusion=True, 

1656 ) 

1657 _matrix_rank_sturm_kernel[(batch_count,)]( 

1658 d, 

1659 e, 

1660 at_arg, 

1661 rt_arg, 

1662 out, 

1663 atol_val, 

1664 rtol_val, 

1665 K=k, 

1666 HERMITIAN=hermitian, 

1667 BIDIAG=False, 

1668 BLOCK=block, 

1669 BISECT_ITERS=32, 

1670 TOL_TENSOR=tol_tensor, 

1671 num_warps=4, 

1672 num_stages=1, 

1673 enable_fp_fusion=True, 

1674 ) 

1675 else: 

1676 if small: 

1677 # 32 < k <= 64, m, n <= 64, non-hermitian: single-program 

1678 # Golub-Kahan bidiagonalization (raw d/e) + the Sturm tail 

1679 # shared with the large-matrix path (fp32 bracket counts 

1680 # from the dd/ee tridiagonal + decisive df64 count from the 

1681 # raw d/e). Linear-domain all the way -- replaces the Gram 

1682 # route for this band (whose sigma^2-domain floor 

1683 # overestimates rank on slowly-decaying spectra). 

1684 d = torch.empty( 

1685 (batch_count, k), dtype=torch.float32, device=input.device 

1686 ) 

1687 e = torch.empty( 

1688 (batch_count, k), dtype=torch.float32, device=input.device 

1689 ) 

1690 ddbuf = torch.empty( 

1691 (batch_count, k), dtype=torch.float32, device=input.device 

1692 ) 

1693 eebuf = torch.empty( 

1694 (batch_count, k), dtype=torch.float32, device=input.device 

1695 ) 

1696 tol2_buf = torch.empty( 

1697 (batch_count,), dtype=torch.float32, device=input.device 

1698 ) 

1699 flag_buf = torch.empty( 

1700 (batch_count,), dtype=torch.int64, device=input.device 

1701 ) 

1702 if not tol_tensor: 

1703 # the Sturm tail kernels take tolerance tensors 

1704 at_arg = torch.full( 

1705 (batch_count,), 

1706 atol_val, 

1707 dtype=torch.float32, 

1708 device=input.device, 

1709 ) 

1710 rt_arg = torch.full( 

1711 (batch_count,), 

1712 rtol_val, 

1713 dtype=torch.float32, 

1714 device=input.device, 

1715 ) 

1716 _fast_launch( 

1717 _matrix_rank_bidiag64_kernel, 

1718 (batch_count,), 

1719 matrix, 

1720 d, 

1721 e, 

1722 m, 

1723 n, 

1724 k, 

1725 BLOCK=64, 

1726 num_warps=4, 

1727 num_stages=1, 

1728 enable_fp_fusion=True, 

1729 ) 

1730 _fast_launch( 

1731 _mr_bidiag_to_tridiag_kernel, 

1732 (batch_count,), 

1733 d, 

1734 e, 

1735 ddbuf, 

1736 eebuf, 

1737 k, 

1738 BLOCK=64, 

1739 num_warps=1, 

1740 num_stages=1, 

1741 ) 

1742 _fast_launch( 

1743 _mr_sturm_big_kernel, 

1744 (batch_count,), 

1745 ddbuf, 

1746 eebuf, 

1747 at_arg, 

1748 rt_arg, 

1749 out.reshape(batch_count), 

1750 tol2_buf, 

1751 flag_buf, 

1752 k, 

1753 BLOCK=64, 

1754 BISECT_ITERS=32, 

1755 num_warps=1, 

1756 num_stages=1, 

1757 ) 

1758 _fast_launch( 

1759 _mr_sturm_final_kernel, 

1760 (batch_count,), 

1761 d, 

1762 e, 

1763 tol2_buf, 

1764 flag_buf, 

1765 out.reshape(batch_count), 

1766 k, 

1767 num_warps=1, 

1768 num_stages=1, 

1769 enable_fp_fusion=False, 

1770 ) 

1771 return out 

1772 if os.environ.get("FLAGGEMS_MR_FAST_PATH") != "1": 

1773 # Exact long-dimension path (DEFAULT): QR-compress to the 

1774 # k x k R factor (backward stable in the linear domain), 

1775 # then bidiag64 + df64 Sturm tail. Slower than Gram on 

1776 # this hardware (the Householder panel is a serial O(k) 

1777 # chain of GM round trips) but exact. 

1778 return _launch_longdim_rank( 

1779 matrix, 

1780 atol_tensor, 

1781 rtol_tensor, 

1782 atol_val, 

1783 rtol_val, 

1784 out, 

1785 m, 

1786 n, 

1787 k, 

1788 rows, 

1789 batch_count, 

1790 input, 

1791 ) 

1792 # Gram (Cube) + tridiagonalization + Sturm count as three 

1793 # separate launches -- fast opt-in (FLAGGEMS_MR_FAST_PATH=1) 

1794 # for long-dimension inputs. The sigma^2 domain loses 

1795 # singular values below ~sqrt(k*eps)*sigma_max (rank 

1796 # overestimation on slowly-decaying low-rank spectra -- 

1797 # documented in the report); the exact path above removes 

1798 # that limitation. 

1799 block = 64 

1800 d = torch.empty( 

1801 (batch_count, block), dtype=torch.float32, device=input.device 

1802 ) 

1803 e = torch.empty( 

1804 (batch_count, block), dtype=torch.float32, device=input.device 

1805 ) 

1806 # The Gram kernel writes every element of the (64, 64) tile, so 

1807 # no zero-fill is needed for it. 

1808 padded = torch.empty( 

1809 (batch_count, block, block), dtype=torch.float32, device=input.device 

1810 ) 

1811 if m >= n: 

1812 pm = triton.cdiv(m, block_m) * block_m 

1813 gpad = torch.zeros( 

1814 (batch_count, pm, block), dtype=torch.float32, device=input.device 

1815 ) 

1816 gpad[:, :m, :n] = matrix 

1817 _matrix_rank_gram_kernel[(batch_count,)]( 

1818 gpad, 

1819 padded, 

1820 PM=pm, 

1821 PN=block, 

1822 TALL=True, 

1823 BLOCK_M=block_m, 

1824 num_warps=4, 

1825 num_stages=1, 

1826 enable_fp_fusion=True, 

1827 ) 

1828 else: 

1829 pn = triton.cdiv(n, block_m) * block_m 

1830 gpad = torch.zeros( 

1831 (batch_count, block, pn), dtype=torch.float32, device=input.device 

1832 ) 

1833 gpad[:, :m, :n] = matrix 

1834 _matrix_rank_gram_kernel[(batch_count,)]( 

1835 gpad, 

1836 padded, 

1837 PM=block, 

1838 PN=pn, 

1839 TALL=False, 

1840 BLOCK_M=block_m, 

1841 num_warps=4, 

1842 num_stages=1, 

1843 enable_fp_fusion=True, 

1844 ) 

1845 _matrix_rank_tridiag_kernel[(batch_count,)]( 

1846 padded, 

1847 d, 

1848 e, 

1849 K=k, 

1850 BLOCK=block, 

1851 num_warps=4, 

1852 num_stages=1, 

1853 enable_fp_fusion=True, 

1854 ) 

1855 _matrix_rank_sturm_kernel[(batch_count,)]( 

1856 d, 

1857 e, 

1858 at_arg, 

1859 rt_arg, 

1860 out, 

1861 atol_val, 

1862 rtol_val, 

1863 K=k, 

1864 HERMITIAN=hermitian, 

1865 BIDIAG=False, 

1866 BLOCK=block, 

1867 BISECT_ITERS=32, 

1868 TOL_TENSOR=tol_tensor, 

1869 num_warps=4, 

1870 num_stages=1, 

1871 enable_fp_fusion=True, 

1872 ) 

1873 return out
