3998 

3999def _launch_matrix_rank(input, atol, rtol, hermitian): 

4000 output_shape = input.shape[:-2] 

4001 m, n = input.shape[-2:] 

4002 k = min(m, n) 

4003 rows = max(m, n) 

4004 is_fp64 = input.dtype == torch.float64 

4005 batch_count = input.numel() // (m * n) 

4006 matrix = input.contiguous().reshape(batch_count, m, n) 

4007 out = torch.empty(output_shape, dtype=torch.int64, device=input.device) 

4008 

4009 if is_fp64: 

4010 # fp64 is unsupported on this backend end to end: aclnn svd_npu 

4011 # is fp32-only, and triton-ascend cannot compile fp64 kernels 

4012 # (verified: the rank1/rank2 closed forms and the fused-Jacobi 

4013 # reference path all die with MLIRCompilationError at kernel 

4014 # compile time). Reject BEFORE any shape dispatch -- and before 

4015 # the scale normalization below, whose pow2 mantissa mask is an 

4016 # fp32-only bit trick -- so every shape fails fast with a clear 

4017 # error instead of a compiler crash. 

4018 raise NotImplementedError( 

4019 "FlagGems Ascend linalg_matrix_rank does not support " 

4020 "float64 inputs (triton-ascend cannot compile fp64 kernels)" 

4021 ) 

4022 

4023 # Scalar tolerances (the common case) are passed to the small-path 

4024 # kernels as scalar arguments, skipping the two fill-kernel launches that 

4025 # materializing (batch,) tolerance tensors would cost. Tensor 

4026 # tolerances, and the large-matrix paths (whose kernels only take 

4027 # tensors), still go through _prepare_tolerances. 

4028 tol_tensor = isinstance(atol, torch.Tensor) or isinstance(rtol, torch.Tensor) 

4029 atol_tensor = rtol_tensor = None 

4030 atol_val = rtol_val = 0.0 

4031 if tol_tensor: 

4032 atol_tensor, rtol_tensor = _prepare_tolerances(input, atol, rtol) 

4033 else: 

4034 atol_val, rtol_val = _tolerance_scalars(input, atol, rtol) 

4035 

4036 # Input scale normalization (mirrors the shared implementation): the 

4037 # Householder algebra squares the matrix scale (w = A.v is 

4038 # O(sigma^2)), so fp32 sum-of-squares overflow for |x| ~ 1e20 and 

4039 # underflow for |x| ~ 1e-30. Normalize each batch matrix by its 

4040 # max-abs and shrink atol by the same factor -- rank = #{sigma > 

4041 # max(atol, rtol*sigma_max)} is invariant under this (rtol is 

4042 # relative). Hermitian reads ONLY the lower triangle, so the scale 

4043 # comes from the lower triangle: garbage in the strict upper triangle 

4044 # is invisible to the computation and must not inflate the scale. 

4045 # The divisor is rounded DOWN to a power of two (fp32 mantissa bits 

4046 # masked off): division by 2^e is exact (pure exponent shift), so the 

4047 # normalization adds no rounding step to ordinary inputs (a plain 

4048 # max-abs division flipped a noise-floor lowrank case: (24,24) rank 12 

4049 # read as 13; exp2(floor(log2(x))) is NOT exact on this backend -- 

4050 # measured 0.5 -> 0.49999997). A masked-to-zero scale (all-zero or 

4051 # subnormal-max matrix) maps to 1, i.e. "no scaling", matching native 

4052 # torch. Small matrices (m, n <= 64) use a single-launch kernel -- 

4053 # the aten chain below costs 5-6 launches, which halves the speedup of 

4054 # sub-millisecond ops (measured: herm 17^2 0.85 -> 0.46). 

4055 # nonzero_flag (batch,) int8 records "the (lower-triangle) max-abs is 

4056 # nonzero" for the negative-tolerance fixup at the end, sparing it a 

4057 # full-matrix tril+amax+amin scan per tensor-tolerance call. Also 

4058 # needed when a nonzero scalar atol gets materialized into tensors by 

4059 # the scaling below. 

4060 need_flag = tol_tensor or atol_val != 0.0 

4061 nonzero_flag = None 

4062 if rows <= 64: 

4063 normed = torch.empty_like(matrix) 

4064 scale = torch.empty((batch_count,), dtype=torch.float32, device=matrix.device) 

4065 if need_flag: 

4066 nonzero_flag = torch.empty( 

4067 (batch_count,), dtype=torch.int8, device=matrix.device 

4068 ) 

4069 with torch_device_fn.device(matrix.device): 

4070 _fast_launch( 

4071 _mr_normalize_small_kernel, 

4072 (batch_count,), 

4073 matrix, 

4074 normed, 

4075 scale, 

4076 nonzero_flag if need_flag else scale, # dummy: not stored 

4077 M=m, 

4078 N=n, 

4079 HERMITIAN=hermitian, 

4080 NEED_FLAG=need_flag, 

4081 BLOCK_R=triton.next_power_of_2(m), 

4082 BLOCK_C=triton.next_power_of_2(n), 

4083 num_warps=1, 

4084 ) 

4085 matrix = normed 

4086 else: 

4087 scale_src = matrix.tril() if hermitian else matrix 

4088 scale = scale_src.abs().amax(dim=(1, 2)) 

4089 if need_flag: 

4090 nonzero_flag = (scale > 0).to(torch.int8) 

4091 scale = (scale.view(torch.int32) & -0x800000).view(torch.float32) 

4092 scale = torch.where(scale > 0, scale, torch.ones_like(scale)) 

4093 matrix = matrix / scale[:, None, None] 

4094 if tol_tensor: 

4095 atol_tensor = atol_tensor / scale 

4096 elif atol_val != 0.0: 

4097 # A nonzero scalar atol becomes per-batch under scaling. The 

4098 # kernels take tolerances either both as tensors or both as 

4099 # scalars, so rtol is materialized alongside (it is relative and 

4100 # needs no division). The common atol == 0 case keeps the scalar 

4101 # fast path: 0 / scale == 0. 

4102 atol_tensor = ( 

4103 torch.full( 

4104 (batch_count,), atol_val, dtype=matrix.dtype, device=matrix.device 

4105 ) 

4106 / scale 

4107 ) 

4108 rtol_tensor = torch.full( 

4109 (batch_count,), rtol_val, dtype=matrix.dtype, device=matrix.device 

4110 ) 

4111 atol_val = rtol_val = 0.0 

4112 tol_tensor = True 

4113 

4114 block_r = triton.next_power_of_2(rows) 

4115 relative_epsilon = 1.0e-15 if is_fp64 else 1.0e-7 

4116 absolute_epsilon = 1.0e-300 if is_fp64 else 1.0e-30 

4117 num_warps = 1 if block_r <= 64 else 4 

4118 # Dummy operands for the ATOL/RTOL pointer arguments when the scalar 

4119 # fast path is active (TOL_TENSOR=False): never dereferenced. 

4120 at_arg = atol_tensor if tol_tensor else matrix 

4121 rt_arg = rtol_tensor if tol_tensor else matrix 

4122 

4123 with torch_device_fn.device(input.device): 

4124 if k == 1: 

4125 _matrix_rank_rank1_kernel[(batch_count,)]( 

4126 matrix, 

4127 at_arg, 

4128 rt_arg, 

4129 out, 

4130 atol_val, 

4131 rtol_val, 

4132 M=m, 

4133 N=n, 

4134 ROWS=rows, 

4135 TALL=m >= n, 

4136 HERMITIAN=hermitian, 

4137 BLOCK_R=block_r, 

4138 TOL_TENSOR=tol_tensor, 

4139 num_warps=num_warps, 

4140 ) 

4141 elif k == 2: 

4142 _matrix_rank_rank2_kernel[(batch_count,)]( 

4143 matrix, 

4144 at_arg, 

4145 rt_arg, 

4146 out, 

4147 atol_val, 

4148 rtol_val, 

4149 M=m, 

4150 N=n, 

4151 ROWS=rows, 

4152 TALL=m >= n, 

4153 HERMITIAN=hermitian, 

4154 BLOCK_R=block_r, 

4155 REL_EPS=relative_epsilon, 

4156 ABS_EPS=absolute_epsilon, 

4157 TOL_TENSOR=tol_tensor, 

4158 num_warps=num_warps, 

4159 ) 

4160 elif k <= _TRIDIAG_MAX_K: 

4161 # fp32 small/medium matrices (any row count): fused kernel / 

4162 # bidiag64 / hermitian padded tridiagonalization / QR-compress 

4163 # for long dimensions -- all linear-domain now. 

4164 _launch_tridiag_rank( 

4165 matrix, 

4166 atol_tensor, 

4167 rtol_tensor, 

4168 atol_val, 

4169 rtol_val, 

4170 out, 

4171 m, 

4172 n, 

4173 batch_count, 

4174 input, 

4175 hermitian, 

4176 ) 

4177 elif ( 

4178 k > _RRQR_MAX_K 

4179 or hermitian 

4180 or rows < _RRQR_FAST_MIN_ROWS 

4181 or os.environ.get("FLAGGEMS_MR_FAST_PATH") != "1" 

4182 ): 

4183 # k >= 256, every hermitian input, compact rows <= 256, and the 

4184 # default mode: use the exact paths. FAST_PATH=1 selects QR only 

4185 # for non-hermitian 65..255 inputs whose long dimension is > 256. 

4186 # hermitian: one-sided Householder tridiagonalization + 

4187 # eigenvalue-domain Sturm count (|lambda| > tol via +/-tol qd 

4188 # chains, decisive pass in df64). general: unblocked Golub-Kahan 

4189 # bidiagonalization + df64 Sturm. Both SVD-accurate. Performance: 

4190 # >= 0.8x torch for k >= 256 (general 1.1x/1.8x at 256^2/512^2, 

4191 # 2.8x at 1024^2; herm 2.0x/3.8x, 7.0x at 1024^2). Some compact 

4192 # 65..255 exact shapes dip below 0.8x, but GM QR is slower there 

4193 # after the register-panel path became uncompilable on CANN 9.1.1. 

4194 if atol_tensor is None: 

4195 atol_tensor, rtol_tensor = _prepare_tolerances(input, atol, rtol) 

4196 if hermitian: 

4197 _launch_tridiag_big_rank( 

4198 matrix, 

4199 atol_tensor, 

4200 rtol_tensor, 

4201 out, 

4202 m, 

4203 n, 

4204 k, 

4205 rows, 

4206 batch_count, 

4207 input, 

4208 ) 

4209 else: 

4210 _launch_bidiag_rank( 

4211 matrix, 

4212 atol_tensor, 

4213 rtol_tensor, 

4214 out, 

4215 m, 

4216 n, 

4217 k, 

4218 rows, 

4219 batch_count, 

4220 input, 

4221 hermitian, 

4222 ) 

4223 else: 

4224 # Non-hermitian 65..255 with rows > 256 and FAST_PATH=1: 

4225 # pure-Triton blocked Householder QR (unpivoted); rank is read off 

4226 # the |R_ii| diagonal. There is no native decomposition fallback. 

4227 if atol_tensor is None: 

4228 atol_tensor, rtol_tensor = _prepare_tolerances(input, atol, rtol) 

4229 _launch_rrqr_rank( 

4230 matrix, 

4231 atol_tensor, 

4232 rtol_tensor, 

4233 out, 

4234 m, 

4235 n, 

4236 k, 

4237 rows, 

4238 batch_count, 

4239 input, 

4240 hermitian, 

4241 ) 

4242 

4243 # torch's tolerance is tol = max(atol, rtol * sigma_max) with NO lower 

4244 # clamp, so tol < 0 is reachable only when BOTH atol < 0 and rtol < 0 

4245 # (elementwise) -- and then every singular value (>= 0) exceeds tol: 

4246 # rank == k for a nonzero matrix. (A zero matrix still gives 0: 

4247 # rtol*0 == 0 lifts tol back to max(atol, 0) == 0.) The in-kernel 

4248 # counts assume tol >= 0 -- the hermitian split #{|lam|>tol} = 

4249 # #{lam>tol} + #{lam<-tol} double-counts the overlap when tol < 0, and 

4250 # the sigma^2-domain paths square tol -- so this corner is fixed up 

4251 # after the fact instead of touching every counting kernel. Two 

4252 # implementation constraints: (a) hermitian reads ONLY the lower 

4253 # triangle, so "nonzero" must be checked on the lower triangle -- 

4254 # garbage in the strict upper triangle is invisible to torch and must 

4255 # not trigger the fix; (b) no Python branch on device data -- a 

4256 # bool(...any()) here would sync the host on EVERY tensor-tolerance 

4257 # call, so the tensor branch applies the (usually no-op) where 

4258 # unconditionally and asynchronously. (A Triton early-exit kernel was 

4259 # tried and abandoned: this backend fails to legalize a masked load 

4260 # combined with any runtime scalar in a vector expression -- unresolved 

4261 # () -> tensor materialization, five variants.) The matrix scan itself 

4262 # is free: the tensor branch reuses the entry normalization's 

4263 # nonzero_flag (the scale is already computed from the lower triangle 

4264 # for hermitian inputs, satisfying (a)), leaving only the tiny 

4265 # (batch,)-sized where. 

4266 if tol_tensor: 

4267 neg_pair = ((atol_tensor < 0) & (rtol_tensor < 0)).reshape(output_shape) 

4268 nonzero = nonzero_flag.reshape(output_shape) != 0 

4269 out = torch.where(neg_pair & nonzero, torch.full_like(out, k), out) 

4270 elif atol_val < 0.0 and rtol_val < 0.0: 

4271 src = matrix.tril() if hermitian else matrix 

4272 nonzero = ((src.amax(dim=(1, 2)) > 0) | (src.amin(dim=(1, 2)) < 0)).reshape( 

4273 output_shape 

4274 ) 

4275 out = torch.where(nonzero, torch.full_like(out, k), out) 

4276 return out

4282def linalg_matrix_rank(input, *, atol=None, rtol=None, hermitian=False): 

4283 """Computes numerical matrix rank (Ascend backend).""" 

4284 logger.debug("GEMS_ASCEND LINALG_MATRIX_RANK") 

4285 _check_input(input, hermitian) 

4286 

4287 output_shape = input.shape[:-2] 

4288 if input.numel() == 0: 

4289 # Native torch validates tolerances BEFORE its empty-input return; 

4290 # match that (complex dtype / wrong device / unbroadcastable tensor 

4291 # tolerances must still raise). 

4292 _validate_tolerance_metadata(input, atol, rtol) 

4293 return _empty_matrix_rank(input, output_shape) 

4294 

4295 return _launch_matrix_rank(input, atol, rtol, hermitian) 

4296

4298def linalg_matrix_rank_tol(input, tol, hermitian=False): 

4299 """NumPy-compatible legacy overload where tol is an absolute tolerance.""" 

4300 logger.debug("GEMS_ASCEND LINALG_MATRIX_RANK_TOL") 

4301 return linalg_matrix_rank(input, atol=tol, rtol=0.0, hermitian=hermitian)

4306 result = linalg_matrix_rank(input, atol=atol, rtol=rtol, hermitian=hermitian) 

4307 return _copy_rank_to_out(input, result, out)

4313 return _copy_rank_to_out(input, result, out)
